sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: No matter how many weddings you've been to,
sentences.zh: 无论你参加过多少场婚礼，

sentences.en: it's hard to shake that contagious feeling of optimism.
sentences.zh: 那种具有感染力的乐观情绪总是很难挥之不去。

sentences.en: Couples pledge to love one another in sickness and in health,
sentences.zh: 伴侣们在生老病死、

sentences.en: for richer, for poorer.
sentences.zh: 无论是贫穷还是富有之时，都承诺相爱一生。

sentences.en: Family members dab tears from their eyes,
sentences.zh: 家人们拭去眼角的泪水，

sentences.en: agreeing that these two people are meant to be together forever.
sentences.zh: 认同这两个人注定永远在一起。

sentences.en: But so many marriages become unhappy.
sentences.zh: 但有那么多的婚姻变得不幸福。

sentences.en: Some dissolve.
sentences.zh: 有些破裂了。

sentences.en: Some end in divorce.
sentences.zh: 有些以离婚收场。

sentences.en: And even the successful ones are not without challenges.
sentences.zh: 即使是那些成功的婚姻也并非没有挑战。

sentences.en: No one would deny that long-term relationships are hard.
sentences.zh: 没有人会否认长期关系是艰难的。

sentences.en: And in fact, there's evidence they're getting harder.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有证据表明它们正变得越来越艰难。

sentences.en: Over the past few weeks, our Love 2.0 series has explored new ways to think about
sentences.zh: 在过去几周里，我们的“爱 2.0”系列探讨了思考以下问题的新方法：

sentences.en: how we engage with romantic partners and spouses.
sentences.zh: 我们如何与浪漫伴侣和配偶进行交往。

sentences.en: We've talked about how to build new bonds with our significant others,
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了如何与另一半建立新的纽带，

sentences.en: how to strengthen the bonds we already have.
sentences.zh: 如何巩固我们已有的纽带。

sentences.en: We've looked at how we respond to our partners' most annoying habits
sentences.zh: 我们探讨了如何应对伴侣最令人讨厌的习惯，

sentences.en: and how we can let go of our desire to change them.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何才能放下改变他们的渴望。

sentences.en: Today, we bring you a classic episode that many listeners have told us is one of their favorites.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们为你带来一期经典单集，许多听众告诉我们这是他们最喜欢的节目之一。

sentences.en: It's about the changing nature of marriage in the United States and other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 它关于美国及世界其他地区婚姻性质的变迁。

sentences.en: Lots of people argue that having these high expectations is problematic
sentences.zh: 许多人认为抱有如此高的期望是有问题的，

sentences.en: and it's harming the institution of marriage.
sentences.zh: 并且它正在损害婚姻制度。

sentences.en: And frankly, among the people who used to argue that is myself.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，曾经持这种观点的人之中就包括我自己。

sentences.en: How our expectations of marriage have evolved
sentences.zh: 我们对婚姻的期望是如何演变的，

sentences.en: and a paradoxical way to achieve more happiness in our relationships.
sentences.zh: 以及在我们的亲密关系中获得更多幸福的一种矛盾的方法。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周收听《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: To understand marriage today, we thought it best to go back to a time and place
sentences.zh: 为了理解今天的婚姻，我们认为最好回到那个

sentences.en: when marriage was very different.
sentences.zh: 婚姻截然不同的时代和地点。

sentences.en: Well, I've been studying the history of family life for many, many years,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我研究家庭生活史已经很多很多年了，

sentences.en: but I specifically got interested in marriage
sentences.zh: 但我对婚姻产生具体兴趣，

sentences.en: as we got into these debates about what traditional marriage was.
sentences.zh: 是在我们卷入关于什么是传统婚姻的争论之时。

sentences.en: That's Stephanie Kuntz.
sentences.zh: 那是斯蒂芬妮·孔茨。

sentences.en: She's an emeritus professor at the Evergreen State College
sentences.zh: 她是长青州立大学的名誉教授，

sentences.en: and the author of the book, Marriage, A History, How Love Conquered Marriage.
sentences.zh: 也是《婚姻史：爱是如何征服婚姻的》一书的作者。

sentences.en: I interviewed her back in 2017.
sentences.zh: 我在 2017 年采访了她。

sentences.en: Stephanie says the earliest marriages had nothing to do with the feelings of two people
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮说，最早的婚姻与两个人的感情

sentences.en: or their attraction to one another.
sentences.zh: 或彼此的吸引力毫无关系。

sentences.en: As you probably know, marriage was much more about economics
sentences.zh: 正如你可能知道的那样，婚姻更多地关乎经济

sentences.en: and acquiring powerful in-laws.
sentences.zh: 以及获得强大的姻亲。

sentences.en: Marriage originally arose in more egalitarian band-level societies
sentences.zh: 婚姻最初出现在较为平等的部落级社会中，

sentences.en: as a way of sharing resources and establishing peaceful relations
sentences.zh: 作为一种分享资源和建立和平关系的方式，

sentences.en: with groups that you might otherwise only see occasionally
sentences.zh: 对象是那些你平时可能难得一见、

sentences.en: and you might not know if they were going to be friends or enemies.
sentences.zh: 并且你可能不知道他们会是朋友还是敌人的人。

sentences.en: It was a way of circulating obligations and goods.
sentences.zh: 这是一种流通义务与货物的方式。

sentences.en: I marry my child off to you, and that means you owe me things,
sentences.zh: 我把我的孩子嫁给你，这意味着你欠我东西，

sentences.en: but I also owe you things.
sentences.zh: 但我也欠你东西。

sentences.en: Stephanie brought up a famous example from history,
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮举了一个历史上的著名例子，

sentences.en: the union between Cleopatra of Egypt and Mark Antony of Rome.
sentences.zh: 埃及的克利奥帕特拉与罗马的马克·安东尼之间的结合。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Taylor as Cleopatra.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·泰勒饰演克利奥帕特拉。

sentences.en: Siren of the Nile.
sentences.zh: 尼罗河的海妖。

sentences.en: This is from a 1963 film version.
sentences.zh: 这出自 1963 年的电影版本。

sentences.en: Richard Burton as Mark Antony.
sentences.zh: 理查德·伯顿饰演马克·安东尼。

sentences.en: Rash, impetuous leader of once invincible legion.
sentences.zh: 曾战无不胜的军团中鲁莽、冲动的领袖。

sentences.en: Dreaded adversary on the field of battle.
sentences.zh: 战场上令人畏惧的对手。

sentences.en: The Hollywood version of the story portrays Cleopatra and Antony
sentences.zh: 该故事的好莱坞版本将克利奥帕特拉和安东尼刻画为

sentences.en: as being very much in love.
sentences.zh: 彼此深爱对方。

sentences.en: But Stephanie paints a slightly different picture.
sentences.zh: 但斯蒂芬妮描绘了一幅略有不同的画卷。

sentences.en: There may have been passion, but it was more passion for power than sexual,
sentences.zh: 当时或许存在激情，但比起性欲，它更像是对权力的激情，

sentences.en: although sexual probably entered into it too.
sentences.zh: 尽管性欲可能也包含在其中。

sentences.en: Cleopatra and Antony's marriage was primarily about strategy.
sentences.zh: 克利奥帕特拉和安东尼的婚姻主要关乎策略。

sentences.en: Rome and Egypt were the two most powerful empires in the world.
sentences.zh: 罗马和埃及是世界上最强大的两个帝国。

sentences.en: So getting them, anybody who got them together
sentences.zh: 因此，把它们联合起来，无论谁能把它们撮合在一起

sentences.en: and got an alliance between them would be unstoppable.
sentences.zh: 并在它们之间建立同盟，都将不可阻挡。

sentences.en: The story goes that Cleopatra was married to her brother,
sentences.zh: 故事传闻克利奥帕特拉曾嫁给她的兄弟，

sentences.en: and without getting into all the details,
sentences.zh: 而不去陷入所有的细节之中，

sentences.en: let's just say she wasn't too happy with that.
sentences.zh: 只能说她对此并不是很高兴。

sentences.en: So she started an affair with Julius Caesar, the ruler of Rome.
sentences.zh: 于是她开始与罗马统治者尤利乌斯·恺撒有了婚外情。

sentences.en: Cleopatra became pregnant.
sentences.zh: 克利奥帕特拉怀孕了。

sentences.en: When the baby was born, he was named Caesarian.
sentences.zh: 孩子出生时，他被命名为恺撒里昂。

sentences.en: The child gave Cleopatra and Caesar a claim to each other's throne.
sentences.zh: 这个孩子给了克利奥帕特拉和恺撒对彼此王位的宣称权。

sentences.en: It was something they both desperately wanted.
sentences.zh: 这是他们两人都极度渴望的东西。

sentences.en: Sounds like an episode of Game of Thrones, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来像是一集《权力的游戏》，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, then Caesar died, and Mark Antony came along.
sentences.zh: 然后，恺撒死了，马克·安东尼出现了。

sentences.en: And, of course, the story tells that she seduced him.
sentences.zh: 当然，故事说她诱惑了他。

sentences.en: But, you know, when you really look at what was happening practically,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当你真正审视实际发生的事情时，

sentences.en: this was another political alliance.
sentences.zh: 这又是另一个政治同盟。

sentences.en: First, as did Caesar, you will marry me according to Egyptian ritual.
sentences.zh: 首先，正如恺撒所做的那样，你将按照埃及的仪式娶我。

sentences.en: It's not a condition, that's a reward.
sentences.zh: 这不是条件，这是奖励。

sentences.en: You will declare by your authority Caesarian to be king of Egypt,
sentences.zh: 你将以你的权威宣布恺撒里昂为埃及国王，

sentences.en: and we will rule together in his name.
sentences.zh: 我们将以他的名义共同统治。

sentences.en: Caesarian was too young to rule, and Antony could rule in his place.
sentences.zh: 恺撒里昂年纪太小无法统治，而安东尼可以代为统治。

sentences.en: So it was a great big political alliance, just like Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的政治同盟，就像《权力的游戏》一样。

sentences.en: This marriage strategy wasn't just for kings and queens.
sentences.zh: 这种婚姻策略不仅仅适用于国王和王后。

sentences.en: There's a common misconception that people of lower classes in this time married for love.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍存在一种误解，认为这个时期的下层阶级是为了爱而结婚。

sentences.en: Not true, Stephanie says.
sentences.zh: 并非如此，斯蒂芬妮说。

sentences.en: You couldn't run a farm with one person.
sentences.zh: 你无法只靠一个人经营农场。

sentences.en: You couldn't run a bakery with one person.
sentences.zh: 你无法只靠一个人经营面包店。

sentences.en: So people who were bakers married other bakers.
sentences.zh: 所以身为面包师的人会与其他的面包师结婚。

sentences.en: If you were a peasant, you wanted somebody who had a good reputation as a hard worker.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个农民，你会想要一个有着勤劳好名声的人。

sentences.en: And that was much more important than this frivolous luxury,
sentences.zh: 这远比这种轻浮的奢侈重要得多，

sentences.en: is the way it was really thought of, as how attracted you were to the person.
sentences.zh: 当时人们确实是这样看待你对这个人的吸引力的。

sentences.en: A different idea started to become more common in the 17 and 1800s.
sentences.zh: 一种不同的观念在 18 和 19 世纪开始变得更加普遍。

sentences.en: Jane Austen, the famous novelist, may well have been the trailblazer.
sentences.zh: 著名小说家简·奥斯汀很可能是开拓者。

sentences.en: For those who don't remember the plot of her book, Pride and Prejudice,
sentences.zh: 对于那些记不清她的书《傲慢与偏见》情节的人，

sentences.en: Mr. Darcy, who has been promised in marriage to his wealthy cousin,
sentences.zh: 达西先生原本被许配给他的富有表妹，

sentences.en: falls instead for Elizabeth Bennet, a woman of modest means.
sentences.zh: 却转而爱上了家境平平的伊丽莎白·贝内特。

sentences.en: That throws his aunt into a rage.
sentences.zh: 这让他的姨妈勃然大怒。

sentences.en: Mr. Darcy is engaged to my daughter.
sentences.zh: 达西先生已经与我的女儿订婚了。

sentences.en: Now what have you to say?
sentences.zh: 现在你还有什么话说？

sentences.en: Only this, if that is the case, you can have no reason to suppose he would make an offer to me.
sentences.zh: 只有这些，如果情况确实如此，你就没有理由认为他会向我求婚。

sentences.en: You selfish girl!
sentences.zh: 你这个自私的女孩！

sentences.en: This union has been planned since their infancy.
sentences.zh: 这段结合从他们儿时起就已经计划好了。

sentences.en: Do you think it can be prevented by a young woman of inferior birth?
sentences.zh: 你以为凭一个出身低微的年轻女性就能阻止它吗？

sentences.en: Heaven and earth, are the shades of Pemberley to be thus polluted?
sentences.zh: 天哪，彭伯利的阴影难道要这样被玷污吗？

sentences.en: Now tell me once and for all, are you engaged to him?
sentences.zh: 现在明确告诉我，你跟他订婚了吗？

sentences.en: I am not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: So, Stephanie, talk about this.
sentences.zh: 那么，斯蒂芬妮，谈谈这个吧。

sentences.en: This is the first glimmers, if you will, of the idea that in some ways love was coming to conquer marriage.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这正是爱在某种程度上开始征服婚姻这一理念的最初微光。

sentences.en: This clip you used is perfect because it illustrates the fact that
sentences.zh: 你用的这个片段非常完美，因为它阐明了这样一个事实：

sentences.en: men found it easier to embrace the love match than women did.
sentences.zh: 相比女性，男性发现接受爱情婚姻更容易。

sentences.en: Men could marry down because they could go out and earn wages.
sentences.zh: 男性可以向下婚嫁，因为他们可以出去挣薪水。

sentences.en: Women had to be very, very cautious.
sentences.zh: 女性必须非常、非常谨慎。

sentences.en: You know, as you could say, my heart inclines to Harry, but, you know, I'd better marry who my parents want me to
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如你可以说的，我的心倾向于哈里，但是，你知道，我最好还是嫁给父母希望我嫁的人，

sentences.en: and the person who is most likely to be able to support me.
sentences.zh: 以及最有可能能够养活我的人。

sentences.en: And so there was a prolonged period of time where men actually were more romantic than women in the courtship arena.
sentences.zh: 因此，在求爱领域，曾有一个相当长的时间段，男性实际上比女性更浪漫。

sentences.en: By the second half of the 19th century, the Jane Austen model of marriage had taken firm hold in the United States.
sentences.zh: 到了 19 世纪下半叶，简·奥斯汀式的婚姻模式在美国已经牢固确立。

sentences.en: The idea of marrying for anything other than love came to be seen as old-fashioned.
sentences.zh: 为了爱以外的任何原因而结婚的观念开始被视为过时。

sentences.en: And with the rise of this new idea came another.
sentences.zh: 随着这种新观念的兴起，另一种观念也随之出现。

sentences.en: If marriage was once seen as a partnership between people from similar backgrounds and similar social classes,
sentences.zh: 如果说婚姻曾被视为背景相似、社会阶层相似的人之间的伙伴关系，

sentences.en: the new model of marriage began to celebrate the coming together of people who were supposedly radically different from one another.
sentences.zh: 那么新的婚姻模式开始赞美那些据称彼此截然不同的人的结合。

sentences.en: And you got this new theory that love was a union of opposites.
sentences.zh: 于是你得到了这样一种新理论：爱是对立面的结合。

sentences.en: Now this idea came that men and women were totally different,
sentences.zh: 现在这种观念随之产生，即男人和女人是完全不同的，

sentences.en: and you could only have access to the emotions, resources, abilities of the other by getting married and staying married.
sentences.zh: 你只有通过结婚并维持婚姻，才能获得对方的情感、资源和能力。

sentences.en: You were incomplete without it.
sentences.zh: 没有它，你就是不完整的。

sentences.en: In practice, this dovetailed with a changing economic landscape in the country,
sentences.zh: 在实践中，这与国内不断变化的经济格局相吻合，

sentences.en: where men increasingly became the breadwinners and women became homemakers.
sentences.zh: 在这个格局中，男性日益成为顶梁柱，而女性则成为了家庭主妇。

sentences.en: The 1950s sitcom Leave it to Beaver makes clear this division between male and female roles.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代的情景喜剧《留给海狸》明确展现了这种男性和女性角色的划分。

sentences.en: You know, Dad, it's funny.
sentences.zh: 你知道，爸爸，这很有趣。

sentences.en: What's funny?
sentences.zh: 有什么有趣的？

sentences.en: Well, whenever we cook inside, Mom always says they're cooking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，每当我们在室内做饭时，妈妈总是说他们在做饭。

sentences.en: But whenever we cook outside, you always do it.
sentences.zh: 但每当我们在户外做饭时，总是你在做。

sentences.en: How come?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's sort of traditional, I guess.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这算是一种传统吧。

sentences.en: You know, they say a woman's place is in the home,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们说女人的归宿是家庭，

sentences.en: and I suppose as long as she's in the home, she might as well be in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 我想只要她在家里，她最好还是待在厨房里。

sentences.en: Well, that explains about Mom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这解释了关于妈妈的事。

sentences.en: But how come you always do the outside cooking?
sentences.zh: 但为什么总是你在做室外的烹饪呢？

sentences.en: Well, I'll tell you, son.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我来告诉你，儿子。

sentences.en: And women do all right when they have all the modern conveniences.
sentences.zh: 当拥有所有现代便利设施时，女人们做得很好。

sentences.en: But us men are better at this rugged type of outdoor cooking.
sentences.zh: 但我们男人更擅长这种粗犷的户外烹饪。

sentences.en: Sort of a throwback to caveman days.
sentences.zh: 有点像对山顶洞人时代的回归。

sentences.en: Talk to me about this idea, Stephanie.
sentences.zh: 跟我谈谈这个想法吧，斯蒂芬妮。

sentences.en: So clearly, gender biases played a role in how we came to think about marriage.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，性别偏见在我们如何看待婚姻这件事上发挥了作用。

sentences.en: Well, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，绝对是的。

sentences.en: But what's interesting about this clip is that the concept of the male breadwinner was unknown before the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 但这个片段有趣的地方在于，男性经济支柱的概念在 19 世纪之前是未曾听闻的。

sentences.en: Women worked in the home, but so did men.
sentences.zh: 女性在家里工作，但男性也一样。

sentences.en: And men didn't go out and bring home the bacon.
sentences.zh: 而且男性并不是外出把生计带回家。

sentences.en: Women helped raise the pig.
sentences.zh: 女性也有份养猪。

sentences.en: Maybe the man butchered it.
sentences.zh: 也许是那个男人屠宰的。

sentences.en: But the woman often cured the bacon and took the bacon to market.
sentences.zh: 但通常是女人来腌制培根，并把培根拿到集市上去卖。

sentences.en: So, again, this was part of this new idea of love that I talked about earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次说明，这也是我刚才提到的那种新型爱情观念的一部分。

sentences.en: The idea that men and women were so different that the man had to do all the outside stuff because the woman couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 这种观念认为，男女差异如此之大，以至于男人必须包揽所有的外部事务，因为女人无法胜任。

sentences.en: And the woman had to do all the inside stuff because the man couldn't do it and wasn't supposed to do it.
sentences.zh: 而女人则必须包揽所有的内部事务，因为男人无法胜任，也不应该去做。

sentences.en: The idea of the love match may have been controversial at firSt.
sentences.zh: 爱情婚姻的观念在最初可能是充满争议的。

sentences.en: But when concerns were raised about how people from different backgrounds would stay together when they didn't have the bond of shared work or the larger framework of a shared community,
sentences.zh: 但当人们开始担忧，背景不同的人在缺乏共同劳动的纽带或共同社区的更大框架时，究竟该如何维系在一起时，

sentences.en: advocates for love marriage said men and women would stay together because they needed one another to feel psychologically complete.
sentences.zh: 爱情婚姻的倡导者表示，男女之所以能长相厮守，是因为彼此需要对方来获得心理上的完整感。

sentences.en: This theory was later appropriated in romantic stories and movies.
sentences.zh: 这一理论后来被浪漫故事和电影所借用。

sentences.en: Think of the saying, opposites attract.
sentences.zh: 想想那句老话：异性相吸。

sentences.en: But as the divorce rate in America surged in the 1970s and 80s, many started to think that what you should look for in a mate was not your opposite,
sentences.zh: 但随着20世纪70和80年代美国离婚率的飙升，许多人开始认为，你在伴侣身上寻找的应该不是你的对立面，

sentences.en: but someone who shared your interests and values.
sentences.zh: 而是那些与你有共同兴趣和价值观的人。

sentences.en: It wasn't quite the same as one baker looking to marry another baker,
sentences.zh: 这不完全等同于一个面包师想娶另一个面包师，

sentences.en: but more along the lines of people marrying others with similar educational backgrounds and similar cultural and political attitudes.
sentences.zh: 而更倾向于人们与拥有相似教育背景、相似文化及政治态度的人结为连理。

sentences.en: You know, it's important to understand that love itself, the definition has changed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，理解爱情本身、理解其定义的改变是很重要的。

sentences.en: It's different today than it was at the beginning of the love match when it was a union of opposites.
sentences.zh: 今天的爱情与爱情婚姻刚出现时异性结合的年代已不尽相同。

sentences.en: And today it's really like a union of people who share so many values.
sentences.zh: 而如今它其实更像是拥有众多共同价值观的人们的结合。

sentences.en: And that's one of the big challenges of love today, because we spent a hundred years trying to get people to see a difference as erotic and the source of love.
sentences.zh: 这也是当今爱情的一大挑战，因为我们花了一百年时间，试图让人把差异视为充满情趣且是爱情的源泉。

sentences.en: And now our big challenge is how do we make equality erotic?
sentences.zh: 而现在我们的巨大挑战是：我们该如何让平等变得充满情趣？

sentences.en: How do you make equality erotic?
sentences.zh: 你该如何让平等充满情趣？

sentences.en: Where is the sizzle in consensus and compromise, in childcare pickups and doctor's appointments, in a lifestyle symbolized by a Honda Civic rather than a flashy Ferrari?
sentences.zh: 当生活被本田思域而非闪亮的法拉利所象征时，共识与妥协、接送孩子和看医生里面，究竟哪里还有激情？

sentences.en: When we come back, we'll answer that question.
sentences.zh: 广告回来后，我们将解答这个问题。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹特。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹特。

sentences.en: We've been talking with historian Stephanie Kuhns about how marriage changed from an institution that was primarily about economic partnerships and political expedience to one based on romantic love.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在与历史学家斯蒂芬妮·孔茨探讨婚姻是如何从一个主要基于经济伙伴关系和政治权宜之计的制度，转变为一个基于浪漫爱情的制度的。

sentences.en: Once this shift took hold in the United States over the course of the 19th century, love marriages became the norm.
sentences.zh: 一旦这种转变在19世纪的美国扎根，爱情婚姻便成为了常态。

sentences.en: Soon, everyone wanted to know the secrets of making love laSt.
sentences.zh: 很快，每个人都想知道让爱情持久的秘诀。

sentences.en: You've seen those documentaries and news stories about elderly couples who've managed to stay together for most of their lives.
sentences.zh: 你一定看过那些纪录片和新闻报道，讲的是那些携手走过一生大部分时光的老年夫妻。

sentences.en: Meet Milt and Leona, sweethearts for life.
sentences.zh: 来认识一下米尔特和利奥娜，一生挚爱。

sentences.en: We've been married 60 years.
sentences.zh: 我们已经结婚60年了。

sentences.en: 60 beautiful years.
sentences.zh: 美好的60年。

sentences.en: When people ask me, how long have you been married?
sentences.zh: 当人们问我，你们结婚多久了？

sentences.en: I truthfully say, not long enough.
sentences.zh: 我会由衷地回答，还不够久。

sentences.en: A heartwarming documentary about the life of a couple that has been together for three quarters of a century, 75 years.
sentences.zh: 这是一部温馨的纪录片，讲述了一对相伴长达四分之三个世纪——75年的夫妻的生活。

sentences.en: There's something that these stories don't tell you.
sentences.zh: 但这些故事并没有告诉你某些事情。

sentences.en: Social psychologist Eli Finkel at Northwestern University has studied the psychological effects of the historical changes that Stephanie has documented.
sentences.zh: 西北大学的社会心理学家伊利·芬克尔研究了斯蒂芬妮所记录的历史变迁带来的心理影响。

sentences.en: Eli is the author of The All or Nothing Marriage, How the Best Marriages Work.
sentences.zh: 伊利是《全部或一无所有：最好婚姻的运作方式》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He has a very dramatic term for the challenge that many couples face today.
sentences.zh: 对于当今许多夫妻所面临的挑战，他有一个非常戏剧化的词。

sentences.en: Modern marriage, he says, runs the risk of suffocation.
sentences.zh: 他说，现代婚姻面临着窒息的风险。

sentences.en: To understand that term, Eli says you have to look at yet another shift that started in the 1960s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 为了理解这个词，伊利表示，你必须看看始于20世纪60和70年代的又一次转变。

sentences.en: We wanted to complement our emphasis on love, achieving love through marriage, with a new emphasis on achieving a sense of personal fulfillment in the way of personal growth.
sentences.zh: 我们希望将对爱情的强调、通过婚姻实现爱情的追求，与一种新的强调结合起来，即在个人成长方面实现个人成就感。

sentences.en: So in the terminology of psychology, we wanted to self-actualize through our marriage.
sentences.zh: 因此，用心理学的术语来说，我们希望通过婚姻来达成自我实现。

sentences.en: We wanted to grow into a more authentic version of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们希望成长为更真实自我的版本。

sentences.en: One example of this comes from the best-selling book by Elizabeth Gilbert about walking out on her husband and trying to create a more meaningful life for herself.
sentences.zh: 其中的一个例子来自伊丽莎白·吉尔伯特的长销书，讲述了她离开丈夫并努力为自己创造更有意义的生活的故事。

sentences.en: We're going to play a few clips from the movies as we chat.
sentences.zh: 在聊天的同时，我们将播放电影中的几个片段。

sentences.en: And this one comes from the movie Eat, Pray, Love, featuring Julia Roberts.
sentences.zh: 这段来自朱莉娅·罗伯茨主演的电影《美食、祈祷和恋爱》。

sentences.en: We'd only bought this house a year ago.
sentences.zh: 我们一年前才买下这栋房子。

sentences.en: Hadn't I wanted this?
sentences.zh: 难道这不是我一直想要的吗？

sentences.en: I had actively participated in every moment of the creation of this life.
sentences.zh: 我积极参与了这种生活创建过程中的每一个时刻。

sentences.en: So why didn't I see myself in any of it?
sentences.zh: 那为什么我在这一切中都看不到自己的影子？

sentences.en: The only thing more impossible than staying was leaving.
sentences.zh: 唯一比留下来更不可能的事，就是离开。

sentences.en: It sounds like she was searching for her true self, Eli.
sentences.zh: 听起来她是在寻找真正的自我，伊利。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: She, in some sense, helps to epitomize both the strengths and the weaknesses of this modern contemporary approach to marriage,
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，她有助于浓缩这种现代当代婚姻方法的优势与劣势，

sentences.en: where we're looking to our spouse, again, not only for love, but also this sense of personal growth and fulfillment.
sentences.zh: 在这种方法中，我们向配偶寻求的不仅仅是爱，还有这种个人成长和成就感。

sentences.en: And for the first time, you start to see cases where people would say, as I think Liz Gilbert would say,
sentences.zh: 并且你第一次开始看到这样的情况：正如莉兹·吉尔伯特可能会说的那样，

sentences.en: that she was in a loving marriage and he was a good man and treated her well.
sentences.zh: 她身处一段充满爱的婚姻中，他是一个好人，对她也很好。

sentences.en: But she felt stagnant and she really wasn't willing to endure a stagnant life for the next 30 or 40 years.
sentences.zh: 但她感到生活停滞不前，她真的不愿意在接下来的30或40年里忍受这种停滞的生活。

sentences.en: And she walked out.
sentences.zh: 于是她离开了。

sentences.en: This would have been unthinkable, of course, 100 years ago, let alone 500 years ago.
sentences.zh: 当然，这在100年前是不可想象的，更不用说500年前了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This would have been a very, very bizarre thing to say.
sentences.zh: 说出这样的话会是一件非常非常怪异的事情。

sentences.en: And marriage, you know, it wasn't really until the 70s that you started seeing no-fault divorce laws.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，婚姻直到70年代左右才开始出现无过错离婚法。

sentences.en: It used to be that you had to prove some type of serious mistreatment like abuse or desertion.
sentences.zh: 过去，你必须证明存在某种严重的虐待行为，比如虐待或遗弃。

sentences.en: And, yes, it's a very modern idea that we are entitled to a sense of real fulfillment and personal growth through the marriage.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常现代的观念，即我们有权通过婚姻获得真正的成就感和个人成长。

sentences.en: And if our marriage is falling short, many of us consider it to be a reasonable option to end the marriage for that alone.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的婚姻达不到要求，我们中的许多人会认为仅凭这一点就结束婚姻是一个合理的选择。

sentences.en: You come up with what I think of as a riff on a very famous psychological concept.
sentences.zh: 你提出了一个我认为是对某个著名心理学概念的改编版本。

sentences.en: Many years ago, Abraham Maslow proposed that human beings have a series of different needs that begin with physical security and end with a search for meaning and fulfillment.
sentences.zh: 许多年前，亚伯拉罕·马斯洛提出，人类有一系列不同的需求，从生理安全开始，到寻找意义和成就感结束。

sentences.en: And you say that a similar hierarchy has come to describe how many Americans think about marriage.
sentences.zh: 而你认为，类似的层级结构也同样描述了许多美国人对婚姻的看法。

sentences.en: Tell me about what you call Mount Maslow.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲你所说的马斯洛山吧。

sentences.en: Well, one of the most exciting things that happened to me in the process of writing the book is I learned a lot about the history and the sociology and the economics of marriage,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在写书的过程中经历的最兴奋的事情之一，就是我了解了很多关于婚姻的历史、社会学和经济学，

sentences.en: particularly reading people like Stephanie Kuntz, because my primary expertise is as pretty much a laboratory psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 特别是阅读了像斯蒂芬妮·孔茨这样的人的作品，因为我的主要专业领域基本上是一个实验室心理学家。

sentences.en: I bring couples into the laboratory and I videotape them interacting and I follow them over time.
sentences.zh: 我把夫妻请进实验室，将他们互动的过程录像，并对他们进行长期跟踪。

sentences.en: But these other disciplines, scholars in these other disciplines adopt a different approach.
sentences.zh: 但其他这些学科，这些学科的学者们采取了不同的方法。

sentences.en: So I realized that marriage had, in fact, changed radically in terms of the way we expect it to fulfill our needs in America, that is.
sentences.zh: 所以我意识到，就我们对美国婚姻满足我们需求期望的方式而言，婚姻实际上已经发生了根本性的变化。

sentences.en: And it used to be that marriage was about basic economic survival.
sentences.zh: 过去，婚姻关乎基本的经济生存。

sentences.en: We've seen that from Stephanie Kuntz and others.
sentences.zh: 我们从斯蒂芬妮·孔茨和其他人那里看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And you can think of that as being at the bottom of Maslow's hierarchy toward the physiological and safety needs, really survival-based needs.
sentences.zh: 你可以认为这处于马斯洛需求层次的底部，朝向生理和安全需求，也就是真正基于生存的需求。

sentences.en: And then as we track marriage and it becomes more about love, now we're more toward the middle of Maslow's hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着我们追踪婚姻的发展，它变得越来越关乎爱情，现在我们更接近马斯洛需求层次的中部。

sentences.en: And then in the 1960s and then really up until today, we're in this new era where, yes, we're still looking for love, but now we're toward the top of Maslow's hierarchy,
sentences.zh: 接着在20世纪60年代，一直持续到今天，我们进入了一个新时代，是的，我们仍在寻找爱，但现在我们处于马斯洛需求层次的顶端，

sentences.en: where he's talking about things like esteem and self-actualization.
sentences.zh: 也就是他谈论诸如尊重和自我实现等事物的地方。

sentences.en: And so our expectations of marriage have basically ascended from the bottom to the top of Maslow's hierarchy over the course of American history.
sentences.zh: 因此，在美国历史的长河中，我们对婚姻的期望基本上从马斯洛需求层次的底部攀升到了顶部。

sentences.en: And one of the ideas that emerged as I was writing this book is that we can conceptualize Maslow's hierarchy not just in terms of a triangle, but in terms of a mountain, right?
sentences.zh: 我在写这本书时浮现的想法之一是，我们可以不仅从三角形的角度，而且从山峰的角度来将马斯洛的需求层次概念化，对吧？

sentences.en: And the advantage of thinking of Maslow's hierarchy as a mountain in this way is that it brings to mind a number of metaphors related to mountaineering.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式将马斯洛的需求层次视为一座山的优势在于，它会让人联想到许多与登山相关的隐喻。

sentences.en: And one thing that we know when we climb up a big mountain is the views get increasingly gorgeous as you get to the top, but the oxygen gets a little thinner.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的一点是，当我们攀登一座大山时，当你到达顶峰时，景色会变得格外壮丽，但氧气也会变得有些稀薄。

sentences.en: And so having a successful experience way up there at the top requires that you are able to invest a lot of oxygen,
sentences.zh: 因此，要在高高的山顶上获得成功的体验，要求你能够投入大量的氧气，

sentences.en: either bring extra oxygen with you on the mountain or invest a lot of time and energy in the marriage to succeed up there.
sentences.zh: 要么在山上随身携带额外的氧气，要么在婚姻中投入大量的时间和精力，才能在那里获得成功。

sentences.en: So to continue your analogy, if we want to get to the top of Mount Maslow, but we have failed to bring our oxygen tanks with us,
sentences.zh: 所以顺着你的类比继续说，如果我们想登上马斯洛山的山顶，却没有带氧气瓶，

sentences.en: that's what leads presumably to what you call the suffocation model.
sentences.zh: 这大概就是导致你所说的“窒息模型”的原因吧。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That is, it's lovely way up there at the top.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在山顶上的风景美不胜收。

sentences.en: And if we're looking to try to achieve not only this sense of love and connection, but also this sense of personal growth and authenticity through the marriage,
sentences.zh: 如果我们不仅希望通过婚姻获得这种爱与连接感，还希望获得个人成长和真实感，

sentences.en: but we're trying to do it on the cheap.
sentences.zh: 但我们又想走捷径。

sentences.en: And that disconnect is what I'm talking about when I talk about the suffocation of marriage.
sentences.zh: 这种脱节就是我谈到婚姻窒息时所指的内容。

sentences.en: What I love about that analogy is it makes physical almost this psychological process, this effect of our expectations.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个类比的地方在于，它将这个心理过程、我们期望带来的这种影响变得几乎具有实体感。

sentences.en: All of us can imagine what it would be like to suddenly wake up one morning and decide, you know, I'm going to run a marathon or I'm going to climb a mountain,
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都能想象，如果有一天早晨突然醒来，决定：“你知道吗，我要去跑马拉松，或者我要去爬山，

sentences.en: a very tall mountain, without really any preparation.
sentences.zh: 一座非常高的山”，而实际上没有任何准备，会是怎样一种情景。

sentences.en: And we would recognize that it's not just difficult to do, but potentially foolhardy.
sentences.zh: 我们会意识到这不仅做起来困难，而且可能极其鲁莽。

sentences.en: That is exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I think if we think about what we're really asking of our marriages these days in terms of the, you know, ambition of these expectations,
sentences.zh: 我想，如果我们考虑到这些期望的宏大程度，想想如今我们对婚姻的实际要求，

sentences.en: then we realize that if we're too tired or lazy to invest in the quality of the relationship, that of course we're not going to be able to make the summit attempt.
sentences.zh: 我们就会意识到，如果我们太累或太懒，不愿为维系关系质量投入精力，那么我们当然无法发起登顶冲击。

sentences.en: Of course, we're not going to be able to succeed in meeting those expectations toward the very high end of Maslow's hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们也无法成功满足马斯洛需求层次最高端那些期望。

sentences.en: And so the book talks a lot about how we can, in fact, align what we're asking of the marriage with what the marriage is realistically able to offer us.
sentences.zh: 因此，这本书探讨了很多我们如何才能真正做到：将我们对婚姻的要求，与婚姻现实中能够提供给我们的东西保持一致。

sentences.en: So there have been a few people, Eli, over the years who've tried to explore the same ideas that you have.
sentences.zh: 伊利，这些年来有一些人试图探索和你相同的理念。

sentences.en: Esther Perel, of course, comes to mind.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特·佩雷尔自然浮现在脑海中。

sentences.en: In her famous TED Talk, she summarizes some of these challenges, and I want to play you a short clip.
sentences.zh: 在她著名的TED演讲中，她总结了其中一些挑战，我想放一小段剪辑给你听。

sentences.en: So we come to one person, and we basically are asking them to give us what once an entire village used to provide.
sentences.zh: 所以我们走向某个人，基本上要求他们给我们过去由整个村庄才能提供的东西。

sentences.en: Give me belonging, give me identity, give me continuity, but give me transcendence and mystery and awe all in one.
sentences.zh: 给我归属感，给我身份认同，给我延续性，但同时还要给我超越感、神秘感和敬畏感。

sentences.en: Give me comfort, give me edge, give me novelty, give me familiarity, give me predictability, give me surprise.
sentences.zh: 给我安慰，给我刺激，给我新鲜感，给我熟悉感，给我可预测性，给我惊喜。

sentences.en: And we think it's a given, and toys and lingerie are going to save us with that.
sentences.zh: 而我们认为这是理所当然的，并觉得玩具和蕾丝内衣就能拯救我们。

sentences.en: So I love that passage, Eli, but you talk about the same idea in your book.
sentences.zh: 伊利，我很喜欢那段话，但你在书中也探讨了相同的理念。

sentences.en: You give the analogy of a woman who once turned to five different friends for important things she needed,
sentences.zh: 你举了一个类比：一个女人曾经向五个不同的朋友倾诉她需要的重要事情，

sentences.en: but once she gets married, she turns to her husband for those same five things, and he's not able to provide all of them,
sentences.zh: 但一旦她结婚了，她就把这同五件事都转向她的丈夫寻求满足，而他却无法提供其中所有的东西，

sentences.en: and she feels now unfulfilled.
sentences.zh: 于是她现在感到无法被满足。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: In the research literature on how we achieve our goals, there's a clunky word called multifinality,
sentences.zh: 在关于我们如何实现目标的研究文献中，有一个生硬的词叫“多重目标性”，

sentences.en: and this is the idea that a given means can serve multiple goals.
sentences.zh: 这个观点是说，给定的某种手段可以服务于多个目标。

sentences.en: So, for example, when I walk to work, that might simultaneously meet my need to get to work,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，当我步行去上班时，这可能同时满足了我去上班的需求，

sentences.en: but also my needs to get some fresh air and get some exercise.
sentences.zh: 但也满足了我呼吸新鲜空气和进行锻炼的需求。

sentences.en: And so this one activity can serve all sorts of functions.
sentences.zh: 因此，这单一的活动可以发挥各种各样的功能。

sentences.en: What's interesting is that's really what we've done to marriage, right,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这确实就是我们对婚姻所做的事情，对吧，

sentences.en: is that marriage for a long time served a set and relatively limited array of different functions for us.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，长期以来，婚姻为我们提供了一组相对有限的各项功能。

sentences.en: And over time, we've piled more and more of these emotional and psychological functions.
sentences.zh: 而随着时间的推移，我们把越来越多的这些情感和心理功能堆积到了婚姻上。

sentences.en: So instead of turning to our close friends and other relatives for nights out on the town,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不再去找密友和其他亲戚进行城里的夜生活狂欢，

sentences.en: for deep, intimate disclosure,
sentences.zh: 不再进行深度的、亲密的倾诉，

sentences.en: to a larger and larger extent, our spouse has replaced a lot of what we used to look to our broader social network to help us do.
sentences.zh: 在越来越大的程度上，我们的配偶已经取代了许多我们过去需要依靠更广泛的社交网络来帮助我们完成的事情。

sentences.en: You know, as I read your book, Eli, I realized that it's not just what we expect from our partners that's changing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伊利，当我读你的书时，我意识到发生改变的不仅仅是我们对伴侣的期望。

sentences.en: We also now expect that we can unlock special things in our partners.
sentences.zh: 我们现在还期望自己能够在伴侣身上激发或解锁特殊的东西。

sentences.en: And this is also reflected in the movies.
sentences.zh: 这一点也在电影中得到了反映。

sentences.en: The 1997 movie, As Good As It Gets, has a scene where a woman who is fed up with, you know, put downs by her,
sentences.zh: 1997年的电影《尽善尽美》中有一个场景：一个女人受够了，你知道的，来自她的、

sentences.en: by the man who's trying to woo her, demands that he give her a compliment.
sentences.zh: 试图追求她的那个男人的贬低，要求他夸夸她。

sentences.en: Okay, here I go.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要开始了。

sentences.en: Clearly a mistake.
sentences.zh: 显然是个错误。

sentences.en: I've got this, what, ailment?
sentences.zh: 我得了这个，什么病来着？

sentences.en: My doctor, a shrink that I used to go to all the time,
sentences.zh: 我的医生，一个我以前经常去看心理医生，

sentences.en: he says that in 50 or 60% of the cases, a pill really helps.
sentences.zh: 他说在50%到60%的病例中，吃药确实管用。

sentences.en: I hate pills.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌吃药。

sentences.en: My compliment is, that night when you came over and told me that you would never have...
sentences.zh: 我的赞美是，那天晚上你走过来告诉我，你永远不会……

sentences.en: Um...
Um, all right, well, you were there, you know what you said.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，你在场，你知道你说了什么。

sentences.en: Well, my compliment to you is...
sentences.zh: 好吧，我对你的赞美是……

sentences.en: The next morning, I started taking the pills.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，我开始吃药了。

sentences.en: I don't quite get how that's a compliment for me.
sentences.zh: 我不太明白这怎么能算对我的赞美。

sentences.en: You make me want to be a better man.
sentences.zh: 你让我想成为一个更好的人。

sentences.en: That's maybe the best compliment of my life.
sentences.zh: 这也许是我一生中听到的最好的赞美。

sentences.en: I found this so revealing in the context of your book, Eli.
sentences.zh: 伊利，在你的书的语境下，我发现这太有启发性了。

sentences.en: Helen Hunt's character is telling Jack Nicholson's character
sentences.zh: 海伦·亨特饰演的角色正在对杰克·尼科尔森饰演的角色说

sentences.en: that the thing that makes her feel really good is not what he does for her,
sentences.zh: 真正让她感觉很好的东西，不是他为她做了什么，

sentences.en: but what she can do to unlock something special in him.
sentences.zh: 而是她能做什么来激发他身上某种特别的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is smitten with her, and his desire for her,
sentences.zh: 没错，他对她神魂颠倒，他对她的渴望，

sentences.en: his being impressed with her and the desire to make her like him more
sentences.zh: 他为她着迷以及想要让她更喜欢自己的愿望，

sentences.en: actually makes him want to grow into a better person.
sentences.zh: 实际上促使他想要成长为一个更好的人。

sentences.en: And in some sense, that's the absolute archetype of what we see in contemporary marriage.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这就是我们在当代婚姻中所看到的绝对原型。

sentences.en: Today, we're looking for our spouse to bring out the ideal version of us,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们期望配偶能激发我们理想中的那一面，

sentences.en: the latent version that's inside of us that we can hopefully grow into with enough time and effort.
sentences.zh: 也就是潜藏在我们内心的那一面，只要有足够的时间和努力，我们有望成长为那样的人。

sentences.en: You have a wonderful term in your book.
sentences.zh: 你的书里有一个非常棒的词。

sentences.en: You call this the Michelangelo effect.
sentences.zh: 你把它叫做米开朗基罗效应。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a term I actually got from my doctoral advisor, Carol Rusbolt.
sentences.zh: 是的，这个词其实是我从我的博士生导师卡罗尔·鲁斯博特那里学来的。

sentences.en: Many of your listeners will know that Michelangelo, when he talked about the sculpting process,
sentences.zh: 你的许多听众都知道，米开朗基罗在谈到雕刻过程时，

sentences.en: talked not in terms of revealing a sculpture,
sentences.zh: 他谈论的不是如何展现一件雕塑，

sentences.en: but in terms of unleashing it from the rock in which it's been slumbering.
sentences.zh: 而是如何将它从沉睡的岩石中解放出来。

sentences.en: So the sculptor's job is not to create something new,
sentences.zh: 所以雕刻师的工作不是创造新的东西，

sentences.en: but merely to refine and buff and polish and maybe scrape away the rough edges
sentences.zh: 而仅仅是修饰、打磨、抛光，也许还要刮掉那些粗糙的边缘，

sentences.en: of what was already nesting within the rock.
sentences.zh: 也就是原本就嵌套在岩石中的东西。

sentences.en: That's a really good metaphor for how partners today try to relate to each other.
sentences.zh: 对于现在的伴侣如何试图建立联系，这是一个非常好的隐喻。

sentences.en: That is, all of us have an actual self, the person that we currently are,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们每个人都有一个真实的自我，也就是我们现在的样子，

sentences.en: but we also have an ideal self, a version of ourselves that's aspirational.
sentences.zh: 但我们也有一个理想的自我，一个我们渴望成为的自己。

sentences.en: Like, what could I maybe become if I could be the best version of myself?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我能成为最好的自己，我可能会变成什么样？

sentences.en: And we look to our partners to be our sculptors,
sentences.zh: 我们寄希望于伴侣成为我们的雕刻师，

sentences.en: to help us until we actually grow toward the best ideal version of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 帮助我们，直到我们真正成长为我们最好的理想版本。

sentences.en: So Eli, do we actually have this power, this power to play sculptor and bring out the best in someone else?
sentences.zh: 伊莱，我们真的拥有这种力量吗？扮演雕刻师并激发别人最好一面的力量？

sentences.en: The answer is yes, we do have this power, but it's not easy to do and not everybody is compatible.
sentences.zh: 答案是肯定的，我们确实拥有这种力量，但这并不容易做到，也不是每个人都合拍。

sentences.en: And sometimes the version of you that you want to grow into isn't the version of you that I want you to grow into.
sentences.zh: 有时你想成长成的那个版本，并不是我希望你成长成的那个版本。

sentences.en: And this is a very delicate dance that we play.
sentences.zh: 这是一支非常微妙的舞蹈，我们在其中翩翩起舞。

sentences.en: And, you know, the best relationships today, the sorts of relationships that I call the all relationships
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如今最好的关系，也就是我所说的“全部”关系，

sentences.en: and the idea of the all or nothing marriage, they're well aligned in this sense.
sentences.zh: 以及全盘婚姻或毫无婚姻的理念，它们在这个意义上是高度契合的。

sentences.en: They're able to bring out the best in each other and connect in a way that facilitates each other's personal growth
sentences.zh: 它们能够激发彼此最好的一面，并以一种促进彼此个人成长的方式建立联系，

sentences.en: and therefore helps to produce a really profound amount of emotional connection and psychological fulfillment.
sentences.zh: 从而有助于产生极其深厚的情感联系和心理满足感。

sentences.en: You know, many marriage experts say that high expectations are the enemy of happiness in marriage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，许多婚姻专家都说，高期望是婚姻幸福的敌人。

sentences.en: You come to a slightly different conclusion.
sentences.zh: 你得出了一个略有不同的结论。

sentences.en: You say that it's true that on average, many marriages might be unhappier today than they were half a century ago,
sentences.zh: 你说，虽然平均而言，今天的许多婚姻可能比半个世纪前更不幸福，但这并非普遍现象。

sentences.en: but that isn't true of all marriages.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有婚姻都是如此。

sentences.en: Who are the exceptions?
sentences.zh: 哪些人是例外？

sentences.en: The exceptions are people who bring those expectations and are able to meet them.
sentences.zh: 例外是那些带着这些期望并且能够满足这些期望的人。

sentences.en: And this is, I think, the crux of the entire issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这才是整个问题的核心所在。

sentences.en: Lots of people argue that having these high expectations is problematic and it's harming the institution of marriage.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为，拥有如此高的期望是有问题的，这正在损害婚姻制度。

sentences.en: And frankly, among the people who used to argue that is myself.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，曾经持这种观点的人中就包括我自己。

sentences.en: I, when I set out to write this book, thought I was writing a book about the decline over time in marriage
sentences.zh: 我当初着手写这本书时，以为我写的是一本关于婚姻随时间衰落的书，

sentences.en: and how we're throwing more and more expectations on this one institution and this one relationship,
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何将越来越多的期望压在这个单一的机构和单一的关系上，

sentences.en: but we're not investing enough time.
sentences.zh: 但我们并没有投入足够的时间。

sentences.en: And therefore, we've really created a seriously problematic approach to marriage.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确实创造了一种严重存在问题的婚姻方法。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until I reviewed these other scientific literatures and learned more about how things have changed
sentences.zh: 直到我查阅了其他科学文献并更多地了解了事情是如何变化的之后，

sentences.en: that I realized that's really half the story.
sentences.zh: 我才意识到这其实只占了故事的一半。

sentences.en: It is true that we are asking a lot more, especially when it comes to these more psychological
sentences.zh: 确实，我们索取了更多，尤其是在这些心理需求

sentences.en: and love-based needs than we did in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 和基于爱的需求方面，远超过去。

sentences.en: But some marriages are able to meet those needs.
sentences.zh: 但有些婚姻能够满足这些需求。

sentences.en: And so what does it mean if you have a marriage that you're looking for to meet these very highest level needs,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你拥有一段你所期望的能够满足这些最高层需求的婚姻，

sentences.en: say, for example, in Maslow's hierarchy, and the marriage succeeds in doing so?
sentences.zh: 比方说，在马斯洛的需求层次理论中，而婚姻成功做到了这一点，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: You're able to achieve a level of fulfillment in the marriage that would have been out of reach
sentences.zh: 你能够在婚姻中达到一种满足感，这种满足感在那种我们甚至根本不试图满足这些需求的时代是遥不可及的。

sentences.en: in an era where we really weren't even trying to meet those types of needs.
sentences.zh: 在那个时代，我们甚至根本不试图满足这些类型的需求。

sentences.en: So at the same time that these high expectations are weighting us down
sentences.zh: 因此，正当我们这些高希冀让我们感到沉重

sentences.en: and making it more difficult to achieve a healthy marriage,
sentences.zh: 并使得建立健康的婚姻变得更加困难的同时，

sentences.en: at the same time that a marriage that would have been acceptable to us in 1950
sentences.zh: 在1950年本会被我们接受的婚姻，

sentences.en: is a disappointment to us today because of these high expectations,
sentences.zh: 由于这些高期望，在今天却成了令我们失望的事物，

sentences.en: those same expectations have placed within reach a level of marital fulfillment
sentences.zh: 而正是这些相同的期望，让我们触及了一种婚姻满足感，

sentences.en: that was out of reach until pretty recently.
sentences.zh: 这种满足感直到不久前还是遥不可及的。

sentences.en: So this idea that some people invest heavily in their marriages at the expense of careers and friends,
sentences.zh: 因此，这种认为有些人为了事业和朋友而大力投资婚姻的观点，

sentences.en: maybe even, you know, their children's activities,
sentences.zh: 甚至可能，你知道的，包括他们孩子的活动，

sentences.en: you say this is perfectly captured in a scene from another movie.
sentences.zh: 你说这在另一部电影的一个场景中得到了完美的体现。

sentences.en: In Sideways, Paul Jammadi's wine connoisseur character explains to his love interest
sentences.zh: 在《杯酒人生》中，保罗·加玛蒂饰演的葡萄酒鉴赏家向他的心上人

sentences.en: the difference between a Pinot and a Cabernet.
sentences.zh: 解释了黑皮诺和赤霞珠的区别。

sentences.en: Why are you so into Pinot?
sentences.zh: 你为什么这么喜欢黑皮诺？

sentences.en: I mean, it's like a thing with you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像是你的某种执念。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Um, it's a hard grape to grow, as you know, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如你所知，这是一种很难种植的葡萄，对吧？

sentences.en: It's, uh, it's thin-skinned temperamental, ripens early.
sentences.zh: 它，嗯，它皮薄、性格敏感、成熟得早。

sentences.en: It's, you know, it's not a survivor like Cabernet,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它不像赤霞珠那样是个幸存者，

sentences.en: which can just grow anywhere and, uh, thrive even when it's neglected.
sentences.zh: 赤霞珠无论在哪儿都能生长，甚至在备受忽视的时候也能茁壮成长。

sentences.en: No, Pinot needs constant care and attention.
sentences.zh: 不，黑皮诺需要持续的照顾和关怀。

sentences.en: You know, and, in fact, it can only grow in these really specific little tucked-away corners of the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，事实上，它只能在世界上那些非常特定、隐蔽的角落里生长。

sentences.en: And, and only the most patient and nurturing of growers can do it.
sentences.zh: 而且，只有最具耐心和培育能力的种植者才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Only somebody who really takes the time to understand Pinot's potential can then coax it into its fullest expression.
sentences.zh: 只有真正花时间理解黑皮诺潜力的人，才能引导它展现出最完美的风采。

sentences.en: Or is there just the most haunting and brilliant and thrilling and subtle and ancient on the planet?
sentences.zh: 或者说，难道它不是地球上最令人难忘、最出色、最令人兴奋、最微妙且最古老的吗？

sentences.en: So, of course, Eli, when we hear this and we're thinking about this in the context of marriage,
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，伊莱，当我们听到这个并结合婚姻的语境来思考时，

sentences.en: why wouldn't we all want to grow Pinot?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不都想种植黑皮诺呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think a lot of us should be pretty careful about Pinot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们很多人对黑皮诺都应该相当谨慎。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that clip does an absolutely masterful job of providing an analogy to how marriage has changed in America in the last, say, 50 years or more.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为那个剪辑在提供一个类比方面做得非常出色，它类比了美国婚姻在过去50年或更长时间里的变化。

sentences.en: It's changed from an institution approximating Cabernet, which can just grow anywhere and thrive even when it's neglected,
sentences.zh: 它从一个类似于赤霞珠的机构——无论在哪里都能生长，甚至在被忽视时也能茁壮成长——

sentences.en: to a much more delicate, fragile institution that requires a lot of, of tending and maintenance.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个更加娇嫩、脆弱的机构，需要大量的照料和维护。

sentences.en: So you ask me, who would ever want anything other than, than Pinot Noir, at least according to how Miles thinks about those grapes.
sentences.zh: 所以你问我，谁会想要黑皮诺以外的东西呢，至少根据迈尔斯对那些葡萄的看法是这样的。

sentences.en: And I would say a whole lot of people might not want to deal with something that fragile and delicate.
sentences.zh: 我会说，很大一部分人可能根本不想去应付那种脆弱而娇嫩的东西。

sentences.en: But, like he says, those of us who get it right, that is, well, and he's, he's talking about the grapes.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如他所说，我们当中那些真正搞懂了的人，也就是，嗯，他在谈论葡萄。

sentences.en: When there's the right grower and the right context, the flavors are just haunting and brilliant and subtle and ancient.
sentences.zh: 当有合适的种植者和合适的背景时，那些风味简直是令人难忘、出色、微妙而古老的。

sentences.en: And what I think he's saying is, this is a high-maintenance grape.
sentences.zh: 我认为他想说的是，这是一种需要高维护成本的葡萄。

sentences.en: It takes a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 这需要大量的功夫。

sentences.en: And if you aren't careful and attentive, you're going to be disappointed in it.
sentences.zh: 如果你不够小心、不够细致，你就会对它感到失望。

sentences.en: It's going to fail you.
sentences.zh: 它会让你失望的。

sentences.en: But if you work hard enough, you can have something truly exquisite.
sentences.zh: 但如果你付出足够多的努力，你就能拥有真正精美的东西。

sentences.en: And that is where we are today with the all-or-nothing marriage.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天全盘或毫无的婚姻所处的现状。

sentences.en: One of the conclusions of your book is that we have, in some ways, two major alternatives when it comes to dealing with this challenge.
sentences.zh: 你书中的结论之一是，在应对这一挑战时，我们在某种程度上有两个主要选择。

sentences.en: That many of us want to be at the top of Mount Maslow, but are not investing the time and effort or the patience to actually get there.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人想要登上马斯洛山的山顶，却没有投入时间、精力和耐心去真正到达那里。

sentences.en: In your own marriage, you describe a trip to Seattle where, in your own analogy, you found yourself starved of oxygen.
sentences.zh: 在你的婚姻中，你描述了一次去西雅图的旅行，用你自己的比喻来说，你发现自己极度缺氧。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We went through a hard time.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了一段艰难的时期。

sentences.en: I, in particular, went through a hard time with the adjustment to parenthood.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我在适应为人父母的过程中经历了一段艰难的时期。

sentences.en: And, frankly, I think that the reason I had a hard time is the sort of stuff that I'm talking about in the book.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我认为我之所以经历艰难时期，正是因为我在书中所谈论的那些事情。

sentences.en: I hadn't sufficiently calibrated or recalibrated my expectations to what life would be like with a newborn.
sentences.zh: 我没有充分校准或重新校准我对有了新生儿的生活会是什么样子的期望。

sentences.en: And the research on this is, in fact, tricky.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点的研究确实很复杂。

sentences.en: Obviously, having a bundle of joy is a wonderful thing.
sentences.zh: 显然，拥有一个快乐之源是一件美妙的事情。

sentences.en: And you love the new baby like crazy and kissing that little fuzzy head is one of the most satisfying things we ever get to do in our lives.
sentences.zh: 你疯狂地爱着这个新生婴儿，亲吻那个毛茸茸的小脑袋是我们生活中最令人满足的事情之一。

sentences.en: But the reality is a recent estimate suggests that it's about 33 and a half additional hours a week of extra time, like of care that goes into that.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，最近的一项估计表明，每周大约需要额外多出33个半小时的时间，比如花在照顾孩子上的额外时间。

sentences.en: And I would ask the couples out there listening who don't have a kid, where would those 33.5 hours a week come from?
sentences.zh: 我要问问正在收听节目的那些还没有孩子的伴侣，每周这33.5个小时是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: And then you're complementing that with some sleep deprivation and, frankly, much less time for emotional connection or sexual connection with your spouse.
sentences.zh: 然后，再加上睡眠剥夺，坦白说，与配偶进行情感连接或性连接的时间大大减少。

sentences.en: And is it any surprise that the research evidence shows that the arrival of the first baby tends to be pretty hard on the quality of the relationship, on the marital satisfaction,
sentences.zh: 研究证据表明，第一个孩子的降临往往会对关系质量、对婚姻满意度造成相当大的打击，这难道还奇怪吗？

sentences.en: for example.
sentences.zh: 例如。

sentences.en: And it was during that period where we took a trip to Seattle to see my closest and longest term friend,
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时期，我们去西雅图看望了我最亲密、交往时间最长的朋友，

sentences.en: one of these life experiences that has always been a source of bliss and joy for me throughout the, you know, 30-some-odd years of my life at the time.
sentences.zh: 这是我当时30多年生命中一直是我的幸福和快乐之源的人生经历之一。

sentences.en: And I was miserable.
sentences.zh: 而我却痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: It turns out that traveling across the country with an eight-month-old is not anything like traveling across the country without an eight-month-old.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，带着一个八个月大的孩子跨国旅行，和不带八个月大的孩子跨国旅行完全是两码事。

sentences.en: And then you're together with your best friend, and there's all the stuff that you used to do.
sentences.zh: 然后你和你的挚友聚在一起，有所有你过去常常做的事情。

sentences.en: But now there's an eight-month-old there, and you're not doing any of those things.
sentences.zh: 但现在那里有一个八个月大的孩子，而你什么也做不了。

sentences.en: And I really had a hard time.
sentences.zh: 我真的度过了一段艰难的时光。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't really exaggerate this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我真的无法夸大这一点。

sentences.en: I really struggled emotionally with the adjustment.
sentences.zh: 我在心理上极力挣扎着去适应。

sentences.en: And I said to my wife, and I regret saying this.
sentences.zh: 我对我的妻子说——我很后悔说出这句话。

sentences.en: It's hard for me to say out loud right now.
sentences.zh: 现在对我来说大声说出来都很困难。

sentences.en: You know, I can endure this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我能忍受这一切。

sentences.en: Like, I can get past this, and I certainly love my daughter.
sentences.zh: 就像，我能挺过去，我当然也爱我的女儿。

sentences.en: But I need to stop trying to have fun because if I'm trying to enjoy my life and I'm trying to enjoy you, I keep end up disappointed.
sentences.zh: 但我需要停止试图去寻找快乐，因为如果我试图享受我的生活，试图享受你，我最终只会不断感到失望。

sentences.en: And she was very upset about that.
sentences.zh: 她对此感到非常难过。

sentences.en: And, you know, I made her cry.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我把她弄哭了。

sentences.en: I'm not proud of this at all.
sentences.zh: 我对此一点也不感到骄傲。

sentences.en: But she cried and thought, what, is this the end of us trying to live a good life together?
sentences.zh: 但她哭了，并想，难道这就是我们努力一起过上好日子的终点吗？

sentences.en: Are we just going to hunker down and be unhappy together?
sentences.zh: 难道我们就要这样蜷缩在一起，共同过着不幸福的生活吗？

sentences.en: But the truth is this ended up being the lowest point, but also the starting of where I started to recover a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，这最终成了最低谷，却也是我开始恢复一点生机的起点。

sentences.en: It took that moment before I started to get serious about making life better again.
sentences.zh: 正是经历了那一刻，我才开始认真对待让生活再次变好的事情。

sentences.en: And one of the major ways I did it was by recalibrating my expectations, yes, but also reinvesting in a way that made sure that I was more connected to my wife than we had been.
sentences.zh: 我做到这一点的主要方法之一，是通过重新校准我的期望，是的，但也通过重新投入，确保我与妻子的联系比以前更加紧密。

sentences.en: And it took some work, and it did require that we lower expectations in some ways and then try to meet those lowered expectations.
sentences.zh: 这需要一些工夫，而且确实要求我们在某些方面降低期望，然后努力去满足这些降低了的期望。

sentences.en: And we were, in fact, able to do it, but it certainly wasn't easy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们做到了，但这绝对不容易。

sentences.en: Eli and other researchers have found that it's not especially easy to fulfill a partner's emotional and psychological needs when you're struggling to pay the bills or working three jobs.
sentences.zh: 伊莱和其他研究人员发现，当你正挣扎于支付账单或身兼三职时，去满足伴侣的情感和心理需求并不是件容易的事。

sentences.en: This might be one reason that the institution of marriage appears to be especially fragile among low-income couples.
sentences.zh: 这可能是婚姻制度在低收入伴侣中显得格外脆弱的原因之一。

sentences.en: When we come back, we're going to look at tangible solutions.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将探讨切实可行的解决方案。

sentences.en: If you can't afford to take your partner on that romantic trip to Paris, but you still want to get to the top of Mount Maslow, we'll show you how to get there.
sentences.zh: 如果你负担不起带伴侣去巴黎进行那场浪漫之旅，但你仍然想登上马斯洛山的山顶，我们将向你展示如何到达那里。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: On today's show...
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中……

sentences.en: Marriage is what brings us together today.
sentences.zh: 婚姻是今天将我们聚在一起的原因。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Marriage.
sentences.zh: 婚姻。

sentences.en: Marriage, that blessed arrangement.
sentences.zh: 婚姻，那个受祝福的安排。

sentences.en: That dream within a dream.
sentences.zh: 梦中之梦。

sentences.en: The priest from that iconic scene in The Princess Bride describes it beSt.
sentences.zh: 《公主新娘》中那个标志性场景里的牧师对此描述得最好。

sentences.en: Or does he?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: We're taking a look at how marriage has evolved over time.
sentences.zh: 我们正在探讨婚姻是如何随时间演变的。

sentences.en: It went from a partnership of necessity to a union of two very different people who need one another's love to be complete.
sentences.zh: 从最初出于需要的伴侣关系，演变成了两个截然不同的人的结合，他们需要彼此的爱才能圆满。

sentences.en: Now, it's gone to the all-or-nothing relationships identified by psychologist Eli Finkel.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这种关系已经变成了心理学家伊莱·芬克尔所指出的全有或全无的关系。

sentences.en: Eli argues that our expectations for marriage, both gay and straight, among rich and poor, have dramatically increased.
sentences.zh: 伊莱认为，无论是同性还是异性婚姻，无论贫富，我们对婚姻的期望都大幅提高了。

sentences.en: Couples who are able to meet these higher expectations are happier than couples have ever been.
sentences.zh: 能够满足这些更高期望的伴侣，比以往任何时候的伴侣都要幸福。

sentences.en: But couples who fall short are unhappier than their counterparts a century ago.
sentences.zh: 但那些达不到要求的伴侣，则比一个世纪前的同行更加不幸福。

sentences.en: If you have follow-up questions or thoughts about these ideas, and you'd be willing to share them with the Hidden Brain audience, please record a voice memo on your phone.
sentences.zh: 如果你对这些观点有后续的问题或想法，并愿意与“隐藏的大脑”听众分享，请在手机上录一段语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Then email it to us at ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 然后将其通过电子邮件发送给我们，邮箱是ideas@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Eli says there are things we can do, what he calls love hacks, to reorient how we think about marriage and make ourselves more fulfilled in long-term relationships.
sentences.zh: 伊莱说，我们可以做一些他称之为“爱情小妙招”的事情，来调整我们对婚姻的看法，让我们在长期关系中获得更多满足感。

sentences.en: Some of your listeners might be fans of Marcel Proust, who argues that mystery is not about traveling to new places, but about looking with new eyes.
sentences.zh: 你们的一些听众可能是马塞尔·普鲁斯特的粉丝，他认为神秘不在于前往新的地方，而在于用新的眼光去观察。

sentences.en: And the love hacks are exactly that.
sentences.zh: 而这些爱情小妙招正是如此。

sentences.en: There are ways that we can try to experience the same relationship, but view it in a different way and therefore be a little bit happier in the relationship itself.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过某些方法去体验同一段关系，但以不同的方式看待它，从而在关系本身中感到稍微幸福一些。

sentences.en: So psychologists have long talked about something called the fundamental attribution error, which is sometimes when we see someone behave in a way that we don't like,
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学家长期以来一直在讨论一个叫做“基本归因谬误”的概念，也就是说，有时当我们看到某人的行为让我们不喜欢时，

sentences.en: there's two ways to interpret it.
sentences.zh: 有两种方式来解释它。

sentences.en: You can either say this person is behaving badly because they're a bad person, or you can say this person is behaving badly because there's something in the context.
sentences.zh: 你可以说这个人表现不好是因为他是个坏人，或者你可以说这个人表现不好是因为有某种情境原因。

sentences.en: There's something happening around him or her that's causing him or her to behave this way.
sentences.zh: 他或她周围发生了某些事情，导致他或她做出这样的行为。

sentences.en: And one of the hacks that you suggest is to reinterpret negative behavior from your partner in a way that's more sympathetic rather than critical.
sentences.zh: 你建议的其中一个小妙招，就是以一种更具同情心而不是批判性的方式来重新解读伴侣的消极行为。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying it's magic.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这是魔术。

sentences.en: I'm not saying it's the easiest thing to do, but I'm saying that with some effort, we can get a little better at this.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这是最容易做到的事，但我的意思是，只要付出一些努力，我们就能在这方面做得更好一点。

sentences.en: So your spouse is late.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的配偶迟到了。

sentences.en: Your spouse is disrespectful.
sentences.zh: 你的配偶很不尊重人。

sentences.en: I mean, ideally not in a huge way, but your spouse does something inconsiderate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最好不是那种极其严重的程度，但你的配偶做了一些考虑不周的事。

sentences.en: You have a lot of control over how that behavior affects you.
sentences.zh: 对于这种行为如何影响你，你其实有很大的掌控力。

sentences.en: And in particular, you have control over whether you want to explain that behavior in terms of something about your spouse that's maybe stable and a characterological assessment.
sentences.zh: 特别是，你可以控制是否要从你配偶身上某种可能稳定且属于性格特征的角度来解释这种行为。

sentences.en: Like, my spouse is always such a jerk.
sentences.zh: 比如，我的配偶总是这么混蛋。

sentences.en: You can try instead to say, look, my spouse was a jerk just now, but he's under a lot of stress at work.
sentences.zh: 你可以试着反过来想，听着，我的配偶刚才确实挺混蛋，但他工作压力太大了。

sentences.en: Or you can think, look, he probably tried the best he could.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以想，听着，他可能已经尽力了。

sentences.en: You know, there was probably some traffic or some crisis at work.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，可能路上遇到了塞车或者工作上有什么危机。

sentences.en: I'm just going to let it ride.
sentences.zh: 我就不跟他在意了。

sentences.en: Now, I'm not saying these are easy things to do because we do have a default to explain other people's behaviors as elements of their character.
sentences.zh: 现在，我并不是说这些都是容易做到的事，因为我们确实有一种默认倾向，把别人的行为解释为他们性格的一部分。

sentences.en: But the fact is, and we should be better at understanding this, there are all sorts of things that contribute to why somebody engaged in one behavior over another behavior.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我们也应该更好地理解这一点，导致某人做出某种行为而不是另一种行为的原因有很多种。

sentences.en: And we have some control over the extent to which we interpret our partner's inconsiderate or rude behavior in a way that's more generous and kind.
sentences.zh: 而且，对于在多大程度上以更宽容、更友善的方式来解读伴侣考虑不周或粗鲁的行为，我们是有一定掌控力的。

sentences.en: And the kinder approach will make us happier in the relationship, and our partner will probably be happier too.
sentences.zh: 更友善的处理方式会让我们在关系中更幸福，我们的伴侣大概也会更幸福。

sentences.en: You also think that having what you call a growth mindset is a useful thing.
sentences.zh: 你还认为，拥有你所谓的“成长型思维”是一件很有用的事。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: So the psychologist Carol Dweck at Stanford, she's developed this idea that people differ in terms of how they think about various attributes.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福大学的心理学家卡罗尔·德韦克提出了这样一个观点，即人们对各种特质的看法存在差异。

sentences.en: So she studies intelligence, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，她研究智力。

sentences.en: And people differ in the extent to which they think intelligence is something that's fixed and stable and you have it or you don't versus it's malleable and it's something that you can develop over time.
sentences.zh: 人们在多大程度上认为智力是固定且稳定的——你生来就有或者没有——还是认为它是可塑的、可以通过时间不断发展的，这些看法因人而异。

sentences.en: Well, it turns out there's a lot of good research now on the extent to which people feel like compatibility in a relationship is something that is fixed.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，现在有很多关于人们如何看待关系中的契合度是否为固定之物的优秀研究。

sentences.en: You know, you could call this a destiny mindset.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可以称之为“命中注定型思维”。

sentences.en: People who think, look, partners are either compatible or they're not, and that's the end of the story, versus more of a growth-oriented mindset who think, look,
sentences.zh: 有些人认为，伴侣要么合得来，要么合不来，这就是全部了；而另一些人则持有更倾向于成长的思维，他们认为，

sentences.en: there's a lot of room where you can develop compatibility.
sentences.zh: 你们有很多空间来培养彼此的契合度。

sentences.en: And, in fact, going through difficulties in a relationship isn't a signal that, oh, my goodness, we're incompatible people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，经历关系中的困难并不是在发出信号，天哪，我们是合不来的人。

sentences.en: It's an opportunity to learn to understand each other better and strengthen the relationship through the resolution of the conflict.
sentences.zh: 这是一个通过解决冲突来更好地了解彼此、加深关系的机会。

sentences.en: And here again, it's not like we have complete control over the thoughts that we have about these things, but we can try to make ourselves adopt a more constructive,
sentences.zh: 在这里同样，我们并不是对这些事情的想法拥有完全的控制权，但我们可以努力让自己采用一种更具建设性、

sentences.en: growth-oriented approach to thinking about conflict in the relationship rather than a more destiny-oriented approach that can often view conflict as a deep sign of incompatibility,
sentences.zh: 更倾向于成长的态度来看待关系中的冲突，而不是那种更倾向于命中注定的态度，后者通常将冲突视为极度不合的标志，

sentences.en: and that's pretty destructive for the relationship.
sentences.zh: 这对关系来说是相当具有破坏性的。

sentences.en: You also talk about more serious alternatives.
sentences.zh: 你还谈到了更严肃的替代方案。

sentences.en: So if people find over time that they are just incompatible with one another and yet they have these high expectations of different things they want from their life,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人们随着时间的推移发现彼此确实合不来，但他们对生活中想要的不同事物又有着很高的期望，

sentences.en: you suggest that one of the alternatives might be to develop systems where people are actually getting different things from different people.
sentences.zh: 你建议其中一个替代方案可能是建立这样一种系统：人们实际上从不同的人那里获得不同的东西。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's the same logic again, right?
sentences.zh: 这还是同样的逻辑，对吧？

sentences.en: So we have this all-or-nothing approach.
sentences.zh: 所以我们采用了这种全有或全无的方法。

sentences.en: We expect these high-level things, and many of our marriages are, in fact, falling short of that.
sentences.zh: 我们期望得到这些高标准的满足，而我们的许多婚姻实际上都未能达到这一点。

sentences.en: So one possibility is that we try to invest more in the relationship, and the second possibility, which we've called love hacks, is how to be more efficient.
sentences.zh: 所以一种可能性是我们试图在关系中投入更多；第二种可能性，也就是我们所说的爱情小妙招，是如何变得更有效率。

sentences.en: But the third possibility, and I actually think we should be pretty serious about this.
sentences.zh: 但第三种可能性，我其实认为我们应该相当认真地对待它。

sentences.en: There's nothing shameful about making these sorts of sacrifices.
sentences.zh: 做出这种牺牲并没有什么可耻的。

sentences.en: We should ask less.
sentences.zh: 我们应该减少索取。

sentences.en: In what ways can we in our own marriage look to the relationship and see, man, like I have been looking to fulfill this sort of need in the relationship for a long time,
sentences.zh: 在我们的婚姻中，我们可以通过哪些方式审视这段关系，然后发现，天哪，我长期以来一直期望在关系中满足这种需求，

sentences.en: and I'm chronically a little disappointed about how we do as a couple and helping to fulfill this sort of need.
sentences.zh: 而对于我们作为伴侣在帮助满足这种需求方面的表现，我长期以来一直有点小小的不满。

sentences.en: Is there some other way that I might be able to meet this need I have, either through some other friends or even on my own?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么别的方法能让我满足这种需求，无论是通过其他朋友还是靠我自己的力量？

sentences.en: And there's some research by the psychologist Elaine Chung that looks at what she calls social diversification.
sentences.zh: 心理学家伊莱恩·钟有一些关于她所谓的“社会多元化”的研究。

sentences.en: Like, can you diversify your social portfolio, if you will?
sentences.zh: 就像，你能不能让你的社会资产组合多元化，如果你愿意这么说的话？

sentences.en: And she looks at the people we turn to when we're feeling emotions that can help us regulate those emotions.
sentences.zh: 她研究的是当我们感受到某种情绪时求助的对象，这些人可以帮我们调节这些情绪。

sentences.en: So to whom do you turn when you're feeling sad?
sentences.zh: 所以当你感到悲伤时，你会向谁求助？

sentences.en: To whom do you turn when you want to celebrate your happiness?
sentences.zh: 当你想要庆祝快乐时，你会向谁求助？

sentences.en: And she assesses how much people look to a relatively small number of people to do all of those things versus a larger number of people.
sentences.zh: 她评估了人们是向相对较少的一群人寻求所有这些满足，还是向更多的人寻求帮助。

sentences.en: And she finds across a range of studies now that people who've diversified their social portfolio, that is,
sentences.zh: 她在现有的多项研究中发现，那些社会资产组合多元化的人，也就是说，

sentences.en: turn to different sorts of people for different sorts of emotional experiences, tend to be a little bit happier.
sentences.zh: 为不同的情感体验求助于不同类型的人，往往会稍微幸福一些。

sentences.en: And so with regard to marriage in particular, we've really lumped a lot of our emotional fulfillment on this one relationship.
sentences.zh: 因此，特别是在婚姻方面，我们确实把大量的精神满足都压在了这段单一的关系上。

sentences.en: And for many of us, we would benefit and our marriage would actually benefit if we asked a little bit less in some respects.
sentences.zh: 对我们许多人来说，如果我们能在某些方面少索取一点，我们自己会受益，我们的婚姻实际上也会受益。

sentences.en: I love the idea of diversification and the analogy with financial diversification.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢多元化的这个想法，以及它与金融多元化的类比。

sentences.en: I mean, so the idea, of course, is that you might have, you know, bonds in your portfolio and they don't do very well and they don't grow a lot, but they're very stable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个想法当然是，你的投资组合里可能有一些债券，它们的表现不是很好，也没有太大的增长，但它们非常稳定。

sentences.en: And then you might have some stocks in your portfolio that, you know, are high growth, but they also have the potential for losing a lot.
sentences.zh: 然后你的投资组合里可能有一些股票，你知道的，它们增长很快，但也有可能血本无归。

sentences.en: And what you're suggesting is that by having different things accomplish different parts of what you need,
sentences.zh: 而你所建议的是，通过让不同的事物来实现你所需的不同部分，

sentences.en: your portfolio as a whole ends up being more stable than if you put all your eggs in one basket.
sentences.zh: 你的整个投资组合最终会比把所有鸡蛋放在一个篮子里更加稳定。

sentences.en: You know, that's right.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And that's a neat way of thinking about it that I hadn't fully processed previously.
sentences.zh: 这是一种精妙的思考方式，我以前并没有完全消化过。

sentences.en: In some sense, what we're doing with marriage these days is we've got a heavily stock-loaded portfolio.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我们如今对待婚姻的做法是，我们的投资组合里塞满了重仓股。

sentences.en: And that means that when the market is up, we make huge gains.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当市场上涨时，我们会获得巨大的收益。

sentences.en: But that's a lot of eggs to put in that one basket.
sentences.zh: 但把那么多鸡蛋放在同一个篮子里风险太大了。

sentences.en: And when the market goes down, we're going to get hit pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 而当市场下跌时，我们会受到相当沉重的打击。

sentences.en: And to some degree, that's also a reasonable metaphor for the self-expressive marriage where we look to one person to fulfill so many of our emotional and our psychological needs.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这也是自我表达型婚姻的一个合理隐喻，在这种婚姻中，我们指望一个人来满足我们众多的情感和心理需求。

sentences.en: The payoff can be huge, but there's a lot of risk.
sentences.zh: 回报可能是巨大的，但风险也很高。

sentences.en: Now, for people to actually consider diversifying their portfolio romantically and emotionally, presumably this also creates stresses on what we think of as marriage.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果人们真的考虑在浪漫和情感上实现投资组合的多元化，据推测，这也会对我们所认为的婚姻造成压力。

sentences.en: So if people are looking outside the marriage for emotional support or other needs, some people are going to say, well, are you really married anymore?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人们在婚姻之外寻求情感支持或其他需求，有些人就会说，好吧，这还算真正的婚姻吗？

sentences.en: I think this is a valid question, and this is a complexity that comes up when you think about how an institution like marriage changes over time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个合理的问题，当你思考像婚姻这样的制度如何随时间变化时，就会出现这种复杂性。

sentences.en: I suspect that if somebody transported from 1750 to today, they might look around and say, whoa, that doesn't look like marriage.
sentences.zh: 我猜，如果把某人从1750年传送到今天，他们可能会环顾四周并说，哇，这看起来一点也不像婚姻。

sentences.en: I don't even really get what you guys are doing.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不太明白你们到底在搞什么鬼。

sentences.en: Or better yet, if we transported back to 1750 and looked at what people were expecting and how little they were looking for personal fulfillment from the marriage,
sentences.zh: 或者更好的是，如果我们穿越回1750年，看看当时人们的期望是什么，以及他们从婚姻中寻求个人满足感的程度是多么微乎其微，

sentences.en: we would be bewildered.
sentences.zh: 我们会感到不知所措。

sentences.en: So one of the more controversial ideas that I play with in the book is when I'm talking about ways that we can ask less of the marriage.
sentences.zh: 因此，我在书中探讨的更具争议性的想法之一，就是谈论我们如何能够对婚姻少做要求。

sentences.en: By the way, when I am doing that, I'm talking about how can we strengthen the marriage by asking less of it.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，当我这么做的时候，我讨论的是我们如何通过对婚姻少做要求来加强婚姻。

sentences.en: One of the places that I consider is in the romantic or sexual domain.
sentences.zh: 我考虑的其中一个领域是浪漫或性爱领域。

sentences.en: So is it reasonable for some people to consider some type of consensual non-monogamy?
sentences.zh: 那么，对某些人来说，考虑某种形式的 consensual non-monogamy（知情同意的多边恋/非一夫一妻制）是否合理？

sentences.en: Now, this is not cheating.
sentences.zh: 现在，这不是出轨。

sentences.en: That's the whole idea of consensual non-monogamy.
sentences.zh: 这正是知情同意的非一夫一妻制的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: This is an understanding that we don't need to have complete monogamy all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是一种共识，即我们不需要一直保持完全的一夫一妻制。

sentences.en: And you can negotiate an alternative.
sentences.zh: 你可以协商出另一种选择。

sentences.en: In fact, among millennials, this is becoming an increasingly common way of thinking about the ideal relationship.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在千禧一代中，这正成为一种越来越普遍的理想关系思考方式。

sentences.en: So this is an ideal option, especially for people who generally are connecting pretty well and they love each other and they're good co-CEOs of the household together,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个理想的选择，特别是对于那些总体上相处得相当好、彼此相爱、并且是优秀的家庭联合首席执行官的人来说，

sentences.en: but they're really struggling to sustain a mutually satisfying sex life together.
sentences.zh: 但他们在维持彼此满意的性生活方面确实遇到了困难。

sentences.en: Those are particularly good opportunities to consider.
sentences.zh: 这些是考虑这种选择的特别好的机会。

sentences.en: Could we reduce some of the disappointment and pressure by opening up the relationship in some ways that we can both agree to?
sentences.zh: 我们能否通过以双方都能同意的某些方式开放关系，来减少一些失望和压力？

sentences.en: It's certainly a high risk option, but it's an option that probably will benefit some relationships.
sentences.zh: 这当然是一个高风险的选择，但它是一个可能会让某些关系受益的选择。

sentences.en: You see that you and your wife, Alison, have developed a shorthand of sorts for the times you want to communicate affection, but are starved of time.
sentences.zh: 你发现你和你的妻子艾莉森已经为那些想要表达爱意却又极度缺乏时间的时刻发展出了一种简写方式。

sentences.en: And it has to do with this song.
sentences.zh: 这与这首歌有关。

sentences.en: That's Paul McCartney at the end of the Abbey Road medley.
sentences.zh: 那是《阿比路》串烧末尾的保罗·麦卡特尼。

sentences.en: It's like a little 23-second bonus track.
sentences.zh: 就像一首23秒的小彩蛋歌曲。

sentences.en: And it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: I haven't heard it in a while, and even as I listened to it as you just played it,
sentences.zh: 我已经有一段时间没听过它了，甚至当我像你刚才播放的那样去听它时，

sentences.en: I sort of teared up a little bit because it's been a very significant song for my wife and me in our marriage.
sentences.zh: 我都有点热泪盈眶了，因为这首歌对我和妻子的婚姻来说意义重大。

sentences.en: When we were first dating, you know, people are falling in love and they often say, I love you or whatever.
sentences.zh: 当我们刚开始约会时，你知道的，人们坠入爱河，经常会说“我爱你”之类的话。

sentences.en: But I was very partial to this idea of belly full of wine, right?
sentences.zh: 但我非常偏爱“满肚子红酒”（belly full of wine）这个主意，对吧？

sentences.en: I want to tell her that I love her a lot, but I got to get a belly full of wine.
sentences.zh: 我想告诉她我非常爱她，但我得先喝他个满肚子红酒。

sentences.en: And eventually saying belly full of wine was our little replacement for I love you.
sentences.zh: 最终，说“满肚子红酒”成了我们代替“我爱你”的小暗号。

sentences.en: And what was neat about the way we used the phrase belly full of wine is it was able to contain like a whole terabyte of information about love and respect and affection in this like one second phrase.
sentences.zh: 我们使用“满肚子红酒”这个短语的妙处在于，它能够在这个仅仅一秒钟的短语里包含整整一太字节关于爱、尊重和情感的信息。

sentences.en: We could turn to each other and just say belly full of wine and just really communicate so much information in that very little, just those few words.
sentences.zh: 我们可以转向彼此，只说一句“满肚子红酒”，就能在那个非常短小、仅仅几个词的瞬间真正传达如此多的信息。

sentences.en: And this is an example of a broader idea that we don't appreciate enough, which is that every marriage has its own culture that has its own language and its own expectations.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更广泛概念的例子，而我们对此的认识还远远不够，那就是每一段婚姻都有其自身的文化，拥有自己的语言和期望。

sentences.en: And we can leverage the features of how culture works to benefit the marriage with a sort of emotional shorthand that can help express affection.
sentences.zh: 我们可以利用文化运作方式的特点，通过某种有助于表达爱意的情感简写来让婚姻受益。

sentences.en: And it can be especially crucial if you're going through a difficult time and maybe things are getting a little hot and maybe you're on the verge of a fight and you can say, hey,
sentences.zh: 如果你正经历一段艰难时期，事情可能变得有些紧张，你可能正处于争吵的边缘，而你可以说，嘿，

sentences.en: baby, belly full of wine.
sentences.zh: 宝贝，满肚子红酒。

sentences.en: And you might be able to diffuse some of what could have been a pretty problematic episode.
sentences.zh: 这也许能化解一场本来可能相当棘手的冲突。

sentences.en: Eli Finkel is a social psychologist at Northwestern University.
sentences.zh: 伊莱·芬克尔是西北大学的社会心理学家。

sentences.en: He is the author of The All or Nothing Marriage, How the Best Marriages Work.
sentences.zh: 他是《全或无婚姻：最好的婚姻是如何运作的》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Eli, thank you so much for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 伊莱，非常感谢你今天来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Do you have a personal story to share about a long-term relationship in your own life that has gone very well or gone very badly?
sentences.zh: 你有没有什么个人故事想分享，关于你生活中长期关系进展得非常顺利或非常糟糕的经历？

sentences.en: If you'd be willing to share the story with the Hidden Brain audience, or if you have follow-up questions, thoughts, or comments about this episode,
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意与“隐藏的大脑”听众分享这个故事，或者你对本期节目有后续的问题、想法或评论，

sentences.en: please find a very quiet room and record a voice memo on your phone.
sentences.zh: 请找一个非常安静的房间，在手机上录一段语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Two or three minutes is plenty.
sentences.zh: 两三分钟就足够了。

sentences.en: Then email the file to us at ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 然后将文件通过电子邮件发送给我们，邮箱是ideas@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Use the subject line marriage.
sentences.zh: 邮件主题请写“婚姻”。

sentences.en: That email address again is ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 再重复一遍邮箱地址：ideas@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: After the break, your questions answered.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，为您解答问题。

sentences.en: Psychologist Jonathan Adler returns to the show.
sentences.zh: 心理学家乔纳森·阿德勒重返节目。

sentences.en: He'll answer listeners' questions about the stories we tell about our lives,
sentences.zh: 他将回答听众关于我们讲述自己生活的故事的问题，

sentences.en: and we'll hear remarkable tales from listeners about how they came to terms with dramatic and difficult moments in their lives.
sentences.zh: 并且我们将听到听众们的精彩故事，了解他们是如何接受生活中戏剧性且艰难的时刻的。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: The first films in history were quite simple.
sentences.zh: 历史上最早的电影非常简单。

sentences.en: A series of moving pictures showed a horse running, a family playing in a garden, and a boxer punching his opponent.
sentences.zh: 一系列动态画面展示了一匹奔跑的马、一个在花园里玩耍的家庭，以及一个拳击手痛击对手。

sentences.en: As the technology developed, so did the complexity of the stories portrayed on screen.
sentences.zh: 随着技术的发展，银幕上展现的故事的复杂性也随之增加。

sentences.en: In the 1902 film A Trip to the Moon, Georges Méliès depicted astronomers who fly to the moon, get captured by aliens, and then escape back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 在1902年的电影《月球旅行记》中，乔治·梅里爱刻画了几位飞往月球的天文学家，他们被外星人抓住，随后又逃回了地球。

sentences.en: As Hollywood evolved into its studio era, the plots of films coalesced into a distinct style with a beginning, middle, and end.
sentences.zh: 随着好莱坞进入制片厂时代，电影的情节融合成了一种具有开端、发展和结局的独特风格。

sentences.en: In most blockbuster movies today, the characters inevitably reach a satisfying conclusion.
sentences.zh: 在当今的大多数大片中，角色们不可避免地会迎来一个令人满意的结局。

sentences.en: Filmmakers with an artistic bent have experimented with different storytelling devices.
sentences.zh: 具有艺术倾向的电影制作人尝试了不同的叙事手法。

sentences.en: The 1950 film Rashomon is about a samurai who gets murdered.
sentences.zh: 1950年的电影《罗生门》讲述了一个武士被谋杀的故事。

sentences.en: It tells the same story from four perspectives.
sentences.zh: 它从四个视角讲述了同一个故事。

sentences.en: They end up being four completely different stories.
sentences.zh: 最终变成了四个完全不同的故事。

sentences.en: The film Memento tells its plot in reverse, while Inception evokes the feeling of a fragmented dream.
sentences.zh: 电影《记忆碎片》以倒叙方式展开情节，而《盗梦空间》则唤起了一种碎片化梦境的感觉。

sentences.en: Please, mind telling your subconscious to take it easy?
sentences.zh: 拜托，能跟你的潜意识说一声放轻松点吗？

sentences.en: My subconscious.
sentences.zh: 我的潜意识。

sentences.en: Remember, I can't control it.
sentences.zh: 记住，我可控制不了它。
