sentences.en: When we watch these films, we're riveted by the characters, the action, and the dialogue.
sentences.zh: 当我们观看这些电影时，我们会被角色、动作和对话深深吸引。

sentences.en: But we often fail to notice that the way the story is told has a fundamental impact on how we feel.
sentences.zh: 但我们常常没有注意到，讲述故事的方式对我们的感受有着根本性的影响。

sentences.en: If Forrest Gump didn't have flashbacks, it would simply be a guy sitting on a bench talking to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 如果《阿甘正传》没有闪回，它就只是一个坐在长椅上跟陌生人说话的家伙。

sentences.en: If Star Wars had started with Luke blowing up the Death Star, it would be a completely different story.
sentences.zh: 如果《星球大战》是从卢克炸毁死星开始的，那将是一个完全不同的故事。

sentences.en: What is true in fiction is true in real life as well.
sentences.zh: 小说中如此，现实生活中也是如此。

sentences.en: How we tell stories, including the stories of our own lives, has profound consequences for our well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们如何讲述故事，包括我们自己人生的故事，对我们的幸福感有着深远的影响。

sentences.en: Whom we include, whom we exclude, and what point of view we take, all these choices alter how we feel about ourselves and the world.
sentences.zh: 我们把谁包含在内，把谁排除在外，以及我们采取什么视角，所有这些选择都会改变我们对自我和世界的感受。

sentences.en: We explored the science of stories and what's known as narrative psychology in a recent episode of Hidden Brain titled
sentences.zh: 在最近一期题为

sentences.en: U2.0, Change Your Story, Change Your Life.
sentences.zh: 《U2.0，改变你的故事，改变你的人生》的《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们探讨了故事科学和所谓的叙事心理学。

sentences.en: Our guest was Jonathan Adler, a psychologist at Olin College.
sentences.zh: 我们的嘉宾是欧林学院的心理学家乔纳森·阿德尔。

sentences.en: Today, Jonathan returns to answer listeners' questions about personal stories and how they shape our lives.
sentences.zh: 今天，乔纳森重返节目，回答听众关于个人故事及其如何塑造我们生活的提问。

sentences.en: Jonathan Adler, welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·阿德尔，欢迎再次来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Jonathan, we're constantly telling ourselves stories, and even small details are important in weaving the narrative of who we are.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我们一直在给自己讲述故事，甚至连一些小细节在编织我们是谁的叙事时也很重要。

sentences.en: I'm going to start by having you tell me the story of your day today.
sentences.zh: 我先请你讲讲你今天的故事。

sentences.en: What happened since you woke up?
sentences.zh: 你醒来后都发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, this morning I got up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，今天早上我起床了。

sentences.en: I helped my kids get off to school.
sentences.zh: 我帮孩子们准备去上学。

sentences.en: They are in fifth and seventh grade, so they are navigating their own autonomy and what they're in charge of, but also attending to the clock.
sentences.zh: 他们分别上五年级和七年级，所以他们正在摸索自己的独立性以及自己负责的事物，同时也得注意时间。

sentences.en: And then I came here to campus, and I had a little bit of time to get some work done.
sentences.zh: 然后我来到校园，有一小段时间处理了一些工作。

sentences.en: I met with my new first-year advisees over lunch to get them oriented, and then I came here to the sound studio to get ready to talk with you.
sentences.zh: 午餐时我见了我新带的大一新生顾问指导对象，帮他们适应环境，接着我来到录音室，准备和你交谈。

sentences.en: I have to confess that one reason we ask people this question sometimes is to establish audio levels and to make sure they're sounding good.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，有时我们问人们这个问题的一个原因是为了调整音频电平，确保他们的声音效果好。

sentences.en: But in the context of this conversation I'm having with you, Jonathan, can you just articulate for a moment why the stories we tell about our own lives are so important?
sentences.zh: 但在我和你进行的这场对话的语境下，乔纳森，你能简要阐述一下为什么我们讲述的关于自己人生的故事如此重要吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: That story, I don't know, meets any kind of criterion for interesting or important story.
sentences.zh: 那个故事，我不知道，它是否符合任何有趣或重要故事的标准。

sentences.en: And in fact, when we look back over our lives, it's often the big moments that stick around.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我们回首往事时，往往是那些重大时刻留存了下来。

sentences.en: But the story that I just told you is really all chronology.
sentences.zh: 但我刚刚讲给你的故事其实全都是按时间顺序来的。

sentences.en: There's not much more to it than that.
sentences.zh: 除此之外也没什么特别的了。

sentences.en: But stories actually play a huge number of roles in our lives at the level of the individual, the level of the interpersonal relationship, but also at the broad cultural level.
sentences.zh: 但故事在我们的生活中实际上扮演着极其大量的角色，在个人层面、人际关系层面，以及广泛的文化层面。

sentences.en: So in my field, we're especially focused on the ways stories provide us with a sense of unity and meaning.
sentences.zh: 所以在我的领域，我们特别关注故事为我们提供统一感和意义感的方式。

sentences.en: So stories integrate us.
sentences.zh: 所以故事将我们整合在一起。

sentences.en: They make us feel like we're the same person across time and across situations.
sentences.zh: 它们让我们觉得自己跨越时间和不同的情况依然是同一个人。

sentences.en: And they help turn the messy flow of life into something meaningful.
sentences.zh: 它们有助于将纷繁的生活流转化为有意义的东西。

sentences.en: But stories are also a vital tool for connection with other people and with communities.
sentences.zh: 但故事也是与其他人及社区建立联系的重要工具。

sentences.en: And stories play a huge role in both maintaining and changing culture.
sentences.zh: 而且故事在维持和改变文化方面都发挥着巨大的作用。

sentences.en: One of your main findings is that the way we tell stories can be just as important as the content of our stories.
sentences.zh: 你的主要发现之一是，我们讲述故事的方式可能和故事的内容一样重要。

sentences.en: For example, there's a lot of significance in where we start our stories and where we end our stories.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们将故事从哪里开始以及在哪里结束，这其中包含着巨大的意义。

sentences.en: You call these the chapter breaks in our stories?
sentences.zh: 你把这些称为我们故事中的章节分界点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's important to remember that we have two roles to play with respect to our life story.
sentences.zh: 重要的是要记住，就我们的人生故事而言，我们有两个角色要扮演。

sentences.en: We are both the main character, but we're also the narrator.
sentences.zh: 我们既是主角，但同时也是叙述者。

sentences.en: So while we only have so much control over the things that happen to us, we have somewhat more control over how we parse those experiences.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然我们对发生在我们身上的事情只有有限的控制力，但我们对如何解读这些经历拥有更多的控制力。

sentences.en: And shifting the chapter breaks of our lives means reframing the beginnings and endings of our experiences.
sentences.zh: 改变我们人生的章节分界点意味着重新构建我们经历的开端和结局。

sentences.en: So while we're living our lives, it's hard to know whether we're towards the beginning of some experience versus towards the end of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们经历生活时，很难知道我们究竟是处于某段经历的初期还是尾声。

sentences.en: But in retrospect, we can sort of make some decisions about how to chunk our lives into episodes.
sentences.zh: 但事后回顾时，我们多少可以对如何将生活划分为各个片段做出一些决定。

sentences.en: And simply moving the beginning or ending of episodes can really recast its meaning.
sentences.zh: 而仅仅移动片段的起点或终点，真的可以重新塑造它的意义。

sentences.en: You describe two kinds of stories that you call contamination stories and redemption stories.
sentences.zh: 你描述了两种你称之为“污染故事”和“救赎故事”的故事。

sentences.en: And both these stories have to do with how we are arranging the chapter breaks of our lives.
sentences.zh: 这两种故事都与我们如何安排人生的章节分界点有关。

sentences.en: Can you explain what these two are, perhaps with some examples, Jonathan?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，你能解释一下这两种故事是什么吗，或许可以举几个例子？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And these are two of many themes that show up in people's stories.
sentences.zh: 这些是人们故事中出现的众多主题中的两个。

sentences.en: Contamination stories are simply good turns bad.
sentences.zh: 污染故事很简单，就是好事变坏了。

sentences.en: And redemption is bad turns good.
sentences.zh: 而救赎则是坏事变好了。

sentences.en: So, you know, all lives have good and bad in them.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，所有人的人生中都有好有坏。

sentences.en: But these themes are very much about where we draw connections and parse the chapter breaks.
sentences.zh: 但这些主题很大程度上关乎我们在哪里建立联系以及如何划分章节分界点。

sentences.en: For example, in the story that I shared with you the last time we talked, it was a story about my experience in college, in studying abroad, and then going into graduate school.
sentences.zh: 例如，在上一次我们交谈时我跟你分享的那个故事中，那是一个关于我在大学、出国留学以及后来进入研究生的经历的故事。

sentences.en: And things had been challenging for quite a while, and I really threw myself into my academic work looking towards graduate school.
sentences.zh: 当时情况已经充满挑战好一阵子了，我一心投入学业，期望能进入研究生院。

sentences.en: And then when I applied to graduate schools, I only got into one of the programs that I had applied to.
sentences.zh: 然后当我申请研究生院时，我只被我申请的项目中的一个录取了。

sentences.en: And at the time, that felt like a big letdown.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这感觉像是一个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: Now, when I look back from a vantage point 20 years later, it's one of the most important turning points in my life.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我以20年后的视角回首时，这是我一生中最重要转折点之一。

sentences.en: I really found my intellectual passion.
sentences.zh: 我真正找到了我的学术热情。

sentences.en: I worked with a graduate mentor who really nurtured my career.
sentences.zh: 我和一位真正培育我职业生涯的研究生导师一起工作。

sentences.en: I met the person who I went on to marry and have children with.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了我后来结婚并育有子女的那个人。

sentences.en: So at the time, I might have cut that experience into a contamination experience where I was working really hard and it didn't turn out.
sentences.zh: 所以在当时，我可能会把那段经历切成一个污染经历，我工作非常努力，结果却不如人意。

sentences.en: But when I move the ending of that story later and incorporate what came afterwards when I started graduate school, the chapter,
sentences.zh: 但当我把那个故事的结局往后延伸，并纳入我开始读研之后随之而来的内容时，这个章节——

sentences.en: the transition from college into graduate school actually turns out to be this redemptive story where my one option turned out to be a fantastic pathway for me.
sentences.zh: 从大学到研究生院的过渡，结果居然变成了这样一个救赎的故事：我唯一的选择最后竟成了我的一条绝佳途径。

sentences.en: The striking thing, of course, here is that the facts of your story are not necessarily changing.
sentences.zh: 当然，这里最引人注目的是，你故事的事实并不一定发生了改变。

sentences.en: It's just where you choose to start and where you choose to stop the story.
sentences.zh: 改变的只是你选择从哪里开始以及选择在哪里结束这个故事。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And actually, even the emotional experience isn't changing, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，甚至连情感体验也没有改变，对吧？

sentences.en: Things were hard and later things were better.
sentences.zh: 事情曾经很艰难，后来情况变好了。

sentences.en: But I could cut up the same exact sequence of not only sort of objective chronological facts, but also the emotions associated with them.
sentences.zh: 但我可以把完全相同的事件序列切割开来，这些事件不仅包含客观的时间顺序事实，还包含与它们相关的情感。

sentences.en: And I could cut up that story into ways that would render it with different thematic arcs.
sentences.zh: 我可以把那个故事切割成不同的方式，从而呈现出不同的主题弧线。

sentences.en: And there's real consequences for that.
sentences.zh: 这会带来切实的后果。

sentences.en: We know from the research that contamination themes in people's stories tend to be associated with worse well-being and redemption tends to be associated with positive well-being.
sentences.zh: 从研究中我们知道，人们故事中的污染主题往往与较差的幸福感相关，而救赎则往往与积极的幸福感相关。

sentences.en: Jonathan, I want to walk you through a story from a listener named Cassandra.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我想带你了解一位名叫卡珊德拉的听众的故事。

sentences.en: Here's the first part of her story.
sentences.zh: 这是她故事的第一部分。

sentences.en: It was in 2005, Thanksgiving weekend, and I was with my family in our home in Texas, and most of us were asleep in bed around midnight when someone came into my garage,
sentences.zh: 那是2005年的感恩节周末，我和家人在德克萨斯州的家中，大约午夜时分，我们大部分人都在床上睡着了，这时有人闯入我的车库，

sentences.en: planted an explosive device, and blew my house up.
sentences.zh: 安放了一个爆炸装置，把我的房子炸毁了。

sentences.en: We were sleeping, but not my daughter, my teenage daughter.
sentences.zh: 我们在睡觉，但我的女儿没有，我的十几岁的女儿没有睡。

sentences.en: She was upstairs sewing.
sentences.zh: 她在楼上缝纫。

sentences.en: The lights went off, and then she saw a flame shoot from our driveway across our U-shaped house to the opposite property.
sentences.zh: 灯熄灭了，然后她看到一束火焰从我们的车道穿过我们U形的房子射向对面的产业。

sentences.en: And she ran down the stairs to wake me and my husband up, and she said, fire, fire.
sentences.zh: 她跑下楼去叫醒我和我丈夫，她说，着火了，着火了。

sentences.en: She screamed.
sentences.zh: 她尖叫着。

sentences.en: She woke us both up.
sentences.zh: 她把我们两个都叫醒了。

sentences.en: I tried to turn my light on, but the power was off, and I couldn't understand why the light wouldn't turn on.
sentences.zh: 我试图开灯，但停电了，我不明白为什么灯打不开。

sentences.en: The house was covered in black smoke.
sentences.zh: 房子里弥漫着黑烟。

sentences.en: My husband and I wound up running across the end of the bed, and we slammed into each other.
sentences.zh: 我和丈夫最终从床头那边跑过去，撞在了一起。

sentences.en: I knocked him out.
sentences.zh: 我把他撞昏了。

sentences.en: I ran out the bedroom door.
sentences.zh: 我跑出卧室门。

sentences.en: I met my daughters at the bottom of the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我在楼梯底部遇到了我的女儿们。

sentences.en: We ran toward the front door.
sentences.zh: 我们朝前门跑去。

sentences.en: My younger daughter reached over my shoulder to touch the door.
sentences.zh: 我较小的女儿把手伸过我的肩膀去碰门。

sentences.en: And you know, if you don't open a door and feed the fire, and I was thinking, stop, drop, and I didn't even get the word rollout before the door exploded inwards.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果不打开门去给火提供氧气，我当时在想，趴下、掩护、滚动，我甚至还没来得及说出“滚动”这个词，门就向内爆炸了。

sentences.en: It knocked me onto my back.
sentences.zh: 它把我撞得仰面朝天。

sentences.en: My dog jumped over my prone body.
sentences.zh: 我的狗从我趴着的身体上跳了过去。

sentences.en: Both of my daughters were now out chasing the dog, and my garage door had exploded, and it was metal.
sentences.zh: 我的两个女儿现在都跑出去追狗了，我的车库门炸裂了，那是金属的。

sentences.en: And shards of the door were whizzing towards their heads like saw blades, and I thought, they're going to be decapitated.
sentences.zh: 门碎片像锯条一样呼啸着飞向她们的头部，我想，她们要被斩首了。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, there's more to the story, but what are you hearing so far?
sentences.zh: 所以，乔纳森，故事还有后续，但到目前为止你听到了什么？

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Thank you, Cassandra, for being willing to share that story, and I'm so sorry that happened to you.
sentences.zh: 卡珊德拉，谢谢你愿意分享这个故事，对于你遭遇这一切我深表遗憾。

sentences.en: This is a highly dramatic moment, and it's certainly setting up the dramatic tension.
sentences.zh: 这是一个高度戏剧化的时刻，它无疑在铺垫戏剧性的张力。

sentences.en: I'm dying to know what happens next.
sentences.zh: 我极其渴望知道接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, I think it's fair to say, Jonathan, that at this point in the story, Cassandra's story is pretty horrific.
sentences.zh: 所以，乔纳森，我觉得可以这样说，在故事的这个阶段，卡珊德拉的故事相当可怕。

sentences.en: No one would actually want to be in Cassandra's shoes.
sentences.zh: 实际上没有人会愿意处在卡珊德拉的境地里。

sentences.en: This is definitely almost a contamination story because it started out with everyone sleeping peacefully at night,
sentences.zh: 这绝对几乎是一个污染故事，因为它的开端是每个人夜里都在平静地睡觉，

sentences.en: and suddenly there's this terrible thing that happens to them.
sentences.zh: 突然间就发生了这样一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: So, let me play you the rest of Cassandra's story.
sentences.zh: 那么，我把卡珊德拉故事的其余部分放给你听。

sentences.en: It picks up from here.
sentences.zh: 从这里开始接上。

sentences.en: Saw blades, and I thought, they're going to be decapitated.
sentences.zh: 锯条，我想，她们要被斩首了。

sentences.en: And luckily the saw blades went around them, by them, over them, and they were untouched.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，锯条绕过了她们，从她们身边掠过，从她们头顶飞过，她们毫发无损。

sentences.en: And I could barely see anything because the next explosion just about blinded me, and it blew up my eardruMs.
sentences.zh: 我几乎什么也看不见，因为下一次爆炸差点把我闪瞎，还把我的耳膜震破了。

sentences.en: But I could barely see someone charging through the neighbor's fences, pulling on his pants.
sentences.zh: 但我隐约看到有人正穿过邻居的栅栏冲过来，一边提着裤子。

sentences.en: It was my neighbor, Jeff.
sentences.zh: 那是我的邻居杰夫。

sentences.en: Jeff, he grabbed my dog, he grabbed my daughter, and he hustled them into his house.
sentences.zh: 杰夫，他抓起我的狗，抓起我的女儿，把她们急忙带进他的屋里。

sentences.en: Then I picked myself up, and then I glanced down the street, and I could see through my near blindness
sentences.zh: 然后我爬起来，朝街那边瞥了一眼，在几近失明的情况下，我看到

sentences.en: the Christmas lights of red and blue lights coming towards me.
sentences.zh: 红蓝两色的圣诞彩灯向我驶来。

sentences.en: Those were fire trucks.
sentences.zh: 那是消防车。

sentences.en: Three hours later, 40 of my neighbors were standing with my whole family and my dog
sentences.zh: 三个小时后，我的40位邻居和我的整个家人以及我的狗一起站在

sentences.en: in the street outside my house, watching my house burn to the ground.
sentences.zh: 我家门外的街上，看着我的房子被烧成平地。

sentences.en: And one of the neighbors got out his best scotch, and they passed it around.
sentences.zh: 其中一位邻居拿出了他最好的苏格兰威士忌，大家传着喝。

sentences.en: And somebody else got me some herbal tea.
sentences.zh: 还有人给我弄来了一些草本茶。

sentences.en: Somebody else gave me a bathrobe.
sentences.zh: 另一个人给了我一件浴袍。

sentences.en: Now, I neglected to say that my husband was naked when he was sleeping.
sentences.zh: 现在，我忘了说，我丈夫睡觉时是赤身裸体的。

sentences.en: And when he came to, and I don't know when that was, and came out of the house, he went and grabbed a bathrobe.
sentences.zh: 当他苏醒过来时——我不知道那是什时候——从房子里走出来时，他去拿了一件浴袍。

sentences.en: And I looked up to this two-story house, and fire was coming out every window like giant orange eyelashes.
sentences.zh: 我抬头看着这座两层楼的房子，火焰像巨大的橙色睫毛一样从每个窗户窜出来。

sentences.en: And there was my husband standing with his back to me, warming his cockles by the fire at the front door.
sentences.zh: 而我的丈夫背对着我站在那里，在前门借着大火取暖。

sentences.en: And he was putting on his bathrobe and tying the silk scotch around his waiSt.
sentences.zh: 他正穿着浴袍，把丝质腰带系在腰间。

sentences.en: It was one of the funniest things I've ever seen.
sentences.zh: 这是我见过最滑稽的事情之一。

sentences.en: So anyway, as we watched the fire, we saw the explosions.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，当我们看着大火时，我们看到了爆炸。

sentences.en: Somebody invited me into the house, our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 有人邀请我进屋，是我们的邻居。

sentences.en: We've all recovered.
sentences.zh: 我们都恢复过来了。

sentences.en: We all are okay.
sentences.zh: 我们都好好的。

sentences.en: And we're better for it.
sentences.zh: 而且我们因此变得更好了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Jonathan, this is an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，这是一个了不起的故事。

sentences.en: Talk about the turn that she makes here.
sentences.zh: 谈谈她在这里做出的转变吧。

sentences.en: It sure is an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个了不起的故事。

sentences.en: And I'm glad that everyone turned out okay.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴每个人最后都安然无恙。

sentences.en: It's kind of remarkable to be able to find any humor amidst this, let alone the poetry of the Christmas lights being the first responders on their way.
sentences.zh: 在这一切中居然还能找到幽默感，这简直非同寻常，更不用说那些作为第一响应者在赶来路上的圣诞彩灯所具有的诗意了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, Cassandra certainly ends this story with a redemptive turn, right?
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，卡珊德拉在这个故事的结尾无疑迎来了一个救赎的转折，对吧？

sentences.en: It all turned out okay.
sentences.zh: 一切都安然无恙地解决了。

sentences.en: And she says at the end, we're even better as a result.
sentences.zh: 而且她在最后说，结果我们甚至变得更好了。

sentences.en: So that is quite something to be able to see that kind of turnaround.
sentences.zh: 所以能看到那种天翻地覆的变化，真的是一件很不寻常的事。

sentences.en: In the wake of such a dramatic and terrible event.
sentences.zh: 在经历了这样一个戏剧性且可怕的事件之后。

sentences.en: Talk a little bit more about the effects of redemption stories on our well-being, Jonathan.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，请多聊聊救赎故事对我们幸福感的影响吧。

sentences.en: So the research demonstrates over and over that when we're able to take negative experiences and find something redemptive in them,
sentences.zh: 因此研究一次又一次地表明，当我们能够接受负面经历并在其中找到救赎的意义时，

sentences.en: that that tends to be good for our psychological well-being.
sentences.zh: 这往往对我们的心理健康有益。

sentences.en: But we live in a rich narrative ecology of stories.
sentences.zh: 但我们生活在一个由各种故事构成的丰富叙事生态中。

sentences.en: There are stories all around us.
sentences.zh: 我们的周围到处都是故事。

sentences.en: And some of those stories exert more influence over our lives than others.
sentences.zh: 其中有些故事对我们生活的影响力比其他故事更大。

sentences.en: So scholars in my field call these potent stories master narratives.
sentences.zh: 所以在我这个领域的学者把这些强有力的故事称为主导叙事。

sentences.en: Master narratives tend to be ubiquitous but invisible.
sentences.zh: 主导叙事往往无处不在却又无形无踪。

sentences.en: We only see them when we bump into them, like when our life story doesn't fit in some way with the master narrative.
sentences.zh: 我们只有在与之发生碰撞时才会注意到它们，比如当我们的生活故事在某种程度上与主导叙事不契合时。

sentences.en: And there's excellent work by Dan McAdams suggesting that redemption is an especially potent American master narrative.
sentences.zh: 丹·麦克亚当斯有一项非常出色的研究表明，救赎是一个特别有力的美国主导叙事。

sentences.en: And I would say especially with cancer patients.
sentences.zh: 我要说，在癌症患者身上尤其如此。

sentences.en: We have a strong master narrative of what it means to be a cancer patient in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在美国，关于成为一名癌症患者意味着什么，我们有着强烈的主导叙事。

sentences.en: Cancer is a battle.
sentences.zh: 癌症是一场战斗。

sentences.en: And it's supposed to show you how strong you are.
sentences.zh: 它本该向你展示你有多坚强。

sentences.en: And that kind of redemptive spin on cancer has two kinds of impacts on patients.
sentences.zh: 而这种对癌症的救赎性解读对患者产生了两种影响。

sentences.en: First, if you get cast against your will in a war story, it's going to influence your behavior.
sentences.zh: 首先，如果你违背意愿被卷入一场战争故事中，它会影响你的行为。

sentences.en: So there's research suggesting that the war metaphor might actually lead people to pay less attention to health-supporting behaviors,
sentences.zh: 因此有研究表明，战争隐喻实际上可能会导致人们减少对健康支持行为的关注，

sentences.en: like drinking and smoking less or eating healthier.
sentences.zh: 比如少喝酒抽烟或吃得更健康。

sentences.en: If you're going into battle, you might not care as much about those things.
sentences.zh: 如果你要奔赴战场，你可能就不会那么在意这些事情了。

sentences.en: But those can actually make a difference to your overall health.
sentences.zh: 但这些其实会对你的整体健康产生影响。

sentences.en: But second, I've talked with cancer patients who don't feel like cancer made them stronger.
sentences.zh: 但其次，我曾和一些癌症患者交谈过，他们并不觉得癌症让他们变得更坚强。

sentences.en: And so if cancer isn't some complex gift in disguise, right, if it just sucks,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果癌症并不是某种伪装成复杂礼物的经历，好吧，如果它只是糟糕透顶，

sentences.en: then not only are you sick, but you're not telling a story about being sick that anyone wants to hear.
sentences.zh: 那么不仅你生病了，而且你讲述生病故事的方式也是没人愿意听的。

sentences.en: And indeed, there is research demonstrating that Americans love to hear redemption stories and don't love contamination stories.
sentences.zh: 事实上，确实有研究表明，美国人喜欢听救赎故事，而不喜欢听污染故事。

sentences.en: So when you narrate your own life in ways that don't fit with cultural master narratives, it can be a double whammy.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你以不符合文化主导叙事的方式讲述自己的生活时，这可能会成为双重打击。

sentences.en: When we come back, can the master narrative that tells us to tell redemption stories become a form of pressure on people who've been through tough times?
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，告诉我们要讲述救赎故事的主导叙事，会不会对那些经历过艰难时期的人构成一种压力？

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Jonathan Adler has found that the way we tell stories changes the way we feel about our lives.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·阿德勒发现，我们讲述故事的方式改变了我们对生活的感受。

sentences.en: He says that when we start stories from a place of success and well-being and end the tale with disaster and tragedy,
sentences.zh: 他说，当我们从成功和幸福的地方开始讲故事，并以灾难和悲剧结尾时，

sentences.en: we are telling what he calls a contamination story.
sentences.zh: 我们讲述的就是他所谓的污染故事。

sentences.en: Things started out great and then turned bad.
sentences.zh: 事情一开始很好，后来却变糟了。

sentences.en: On the other hand, when we tell stories that start out with difficulty and challenge but end in a positive place,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，当我们讲述的故事以困难和挑战开局，但最终以积极的结果收尾时，

sentences.en: these redemption stories are often associated with better well-being.
sentences.zh: 这些救赎故事通常与更好的幸福感息息相关。

sentences.en: Jonathan, we heard from a listener who said that the pressure to tell redemption stories can sometimes feel unfair.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我们听到一位听众说，讲述救赎故事的压力有时会让人觉得不公平。

sentences.en: Here's Kristen.
sentences.zh: 听听克里斯滕怎么说。

sentences.en: Since my children were young, I've lost both my parents to cancer,
sentences.zh: 自从我的孩子还小的时候起，我的父母就双双因癌症离世，

sentences.en: had to manage the business of death and of grieving on my own as being an only child.
sentences.zh: 作为独生子女，我不得不独自处理生死和悲伤的事务。

sentences.en: And my children also had witnessed a violent attack that happened on the porch of our old home.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子们还目睹了发生在我们老家门廊上的一起暴力袭击事件。

sentences.en: I also found out that I had two rare medical conditions.
sentences.zh: 我还发现自己患有两种罕见的疾病。

sentences.en: One of them took a few years and a lot of stress to get diagnosed,
sentences.zh: 其中一种花了几年时间承受了巨大压力才被诊断出来，

sentences.en: and the other one just requires a lot of stressful surveillance.
sentences.zh: 而另一种则需要进行大量充满压力的监测。

sentences.en: So this is just a short part of the liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是这份清单上的一小部分。

sentences.en: But I definitely felt the pressure for a redemptive spin on my life.
sentences.zh: 但我确实感受到了要给自己的生活赋予一种救赎色彩的压力。

sentences.en: Basically, I spent my last several years just dealing with the fallout of this.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我过去的几年时间都在应付这一切带来的余波。

sentences.en: I have no elevator pitch to give to people at parties about, you know,
sentences.zh: 我在派对上没办法跟别人简要介绍说，你知道的，

sentences.en: how my life has somehow come to a meaningful culmination out of all of this.
sentences.zh: 我的生活是如何历经这一切最终走向一个有意义的结局的。

sentences.en: But, you know, I guess what's gotten me through is just that I realized that we were hit by an onslaught of events
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我想支撑我度过难关的仅仅是我意识到我们遭遇了一连串的事件，

sentences.en: that were most of which were out of our control.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分都是我们无法控制的。

sentences.en: And we bear the scars, but we're still putting one foot in front of the other,
sentences.zh: 我们带着伤疤，但我们仍在艰难前行，

sentences.en: and our story is still continuing.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事仍在继续。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, you were talking a moment ago about how, in some ways,
sentences.zh: 那么，乔纳森，你刚才谈到在某种程度上，

sentences.en: we have this master narrative that we're supposed to come up with a redemption story.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种主导叙事，认为我们必须想出一个救赎的故事。

sentences.en: And I feel I can very much hear that in the way Kristen is telling the story
sentences.zh: 我觉得我能非常强烈地从克里斯滕讲述她一生中遇到的诸多挑战的故事中听到这一点。

sentences.en: of the many challenges she has encountered in her life.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕，听到这些我感到非常遗憾。

sentences.en: Kristen, I am so sorry to hear about this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道听众们有什么感觉，但仅仅听到克里斯滕所经历的一切，我的身体就有了不同的感受。

sentences.en: I don't know how listeners are feeling, but my body feels different just hearing what Kristen has been through.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很感激能分享这个艰难的故事。

sentences.en: So I'm really grateful for sharing this hard story.
sentences.zh: 我认为记住负面经历是每个人生活的一部分真的很重要。

sentences.en: I think it's really important to remember that negative experiences are a part of everyone's life.
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是忽视它们，就会错失从它们中成长的一次机会。

sentences.en: And if we just ignore them, we miss out on an invitation to grow from them.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经讨论过主导叙事，并将救赎视为美国主导叙事的一个例子。

sentences.en: But we've already talked about master narratives and looked at redemption as one example of an American master narrative.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们的文化中，人们有一种急于求成、渴望救赎的冲动，我们希望尽快摆脱负面情绪，

sentences.en: And I think there's a real rush to redemption in our culture where we want to get through the negative as quickly as possible,
sentences.zh: 给它系上一个漂亮的救赎蝴蝶结然后继续前行。

sentences.en: put a nice redemptive bow on it and move on.
sentences.zh: 但负面经历也能迫使我们跳出那种我们已经习惯了的生活故事。

sentences.en: But negative experiences can also force us out of the story that we've sort of gotten used to living.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，它们可以提供一个以不同视角看待事物的契机。

sentences.en: And in doing so, they can offer an invitation to see things differently.
sentences.zh: 我想明确指出的是，看待事物的新方式并不一定感觉良好，对吧？

sentences.en: I want to be really clear that different ways of seeing things don't necessarily feel good, right?
sentences.zh: 有些事情就是糟糕透顶，我们只需要承认它们在我们生活中的作用，而不需要把它们转化为积极的东西。

sentences.en: Some things are just awful and we just need to acknowledge their role in our lives without needing to transform them into something positive.
sentences.zh: 但即使感觉良好不是一种选择，我们也能找到意义。

sentences.en: But even when feeling good isn't an option, we can find meaning.
sentences.zh: 而这种对意义的积极寻找，听起来正是克里斯滕一直在努力做的事情。

sentences.en: And that active search for meaning is what it sounds like Kristen has been working to do.
sentences.zh: 这本身就是一个值得追求且有价值的目标。

sentences.en: And that in and of itself is a worthwhile and valuable goal.
sentences.zh: 在经历负面事件后，救赎并不是唯一的选择。

sentences.en: Redemption isn't the only option in the wake of negative experiences.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你提到这一点，乔纳森，因为当克里斯滕说时，我深受触动：

sentences.en: I'm so glad you mentioned that, Jonathan, because I was struck when Kristen said,
sentences.zh: “知道有些事情是我无法控制的，这让我感觉好多了。”

sentences.en: I feel better knowing some things are out of my control.
sentences.zh: 所以她不一定是在讲述一个生活发生戏剧性好转的故事，

sentences.en: So she's not necessarily telling a story that says things have taken a dramatic upswing,
sentences.zh: 但她是在说，由于这些负面经历，她对自己人生的理解已经改变了。

sentences.en: but she is saying her own understanding about her life has changed as a result of these negative experiences.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们从某种技术层面审视和检查她的叙事，

sentences.en: So if we were sort of technically looking, examining her narrative,
sentences.zh: 我们可能会看到我们所谓的探索性加工的证据，

sentences.en: we might see evidence of what we call exploratory processing,
sentences.zh: 也就是对意义的寻找，这与救赎不同，对吧？

sentences.en: that search for meaning, which is different than redemption, right?
sentences.zh: 救赎将消极转化为积极。

sentences.en: Redemption turns negative positive.
sentences.zh: 探索性加工可以让我们产生一种意义感，但它可能不会让人感觉良好。

sentences.en: Exploratory processing can lead us to a sense of meaningfulness, but it might not feel good.
sentences.zh: 但对意义的这种寻找依然是一个非常值得追求的过程。

sentences.en: But that search for meaning is still a really worthwhile pursuit.
sentences.zh: 我们从许多听众那里听到的一个常见故事与受伤或生病有关。

sentences.en: One common story we heard from many listeners had to do with an injury or an illness.
sentences.zh: 这是来自埃里森的故事。

sentences.en: Here's one from Allison.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己是一个非常积极的人，我认为部分原因在于我以一种救赎的方式讲述了我人生中的重大故事。

sentences.en: I think I'm a pretty positive person, and I think part of that is telling my big life stories in a redemptive way.
sentences.zh: 大约一年半前，我丈夫被诊断出患有三期结肠癌，

sentences.en: About a year and a half ago, my husband was diagnosed with stage 3 colon cancer,
sentences.zh: 我想我们当时觉得这非常可怕且糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: and I think we sort of thought it was very scary and crappy.
sentences.zh: 但我们做了必须做的事来度过难关，现在我们只觉得他恢复健康真是太幸运了，

sentences.en: But we did what we had to do to get through it, and now we just feel so lucky that he's healthy,
sentences.zh: 而且据我们所知，他已经没有癌症了。

sentences.en: and as far as we know, he's cancer-free.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们生活中非常艰难的一段时期，但我们挺了过来，

sentences.en: So it was a really tough time in our lives, but we came out the other side,
sentences.zh: 我想这只会让我们更加感激彼此。

sentences.en: and I think it just makes us more grateful for each other.
sentences.zh: 所以，乔纳森，埃里森的故事显然是一个救赎故事，从她的讲述方式来看是这样的，

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, Allison's story is clearly a redemption story, the way she's telling it,
sentences.zh: 但我在想，有没有可能有时我们需要让一些时间过去，

sentences.en: but I'm wondering, is it possible that sometimes we need to let some time pass
sentences.zh: 然后才能看到故事中的救赎弧线？

sentences.en: before we can see the redemption arc of a story?
sentences.zh: 当埃里森和她的丈夫正处于应对这场癌症的水深火热之中时，

sentences.en: When Allison and her husband were in the midst of dealing with this cancer,
sentences.zh: 通过救赎的镜头来看待这个故事可能更难一些。

sentences.en: it's possible that it might have been harder to see the story through a redemptive lens.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想确实如此，在与许多癌症患者及其亲属交谈过后我有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, I imagine that's true, having talked with many cancer patients and their loved ones.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我甚至在想埃里森和她的丈夫是否曾被强行推入某种癌症的主导叙事中，

sentences.en: And indeed, I wonder if Allison and her husband felt pushed into, you know,
sentences.zh: 这种叙事在一开始其实并非关于救赎。

sentences.en: sort of a cancer master narrative, which is really not about redemption at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 结局总是伴随着救赎的承诺。

sentences.en: There's always the promise of redemption at the end.
sentences.zh: 但那种故事真正聚焦的是另一个主题，我们称之为自主性，

sentences.en: But that kind of story really centers a different theme, which we call agency,
sentences.zh: 也就是你在多大程度上掌握着自己生活的主动权，

sentences.en: which is sort of the degree to which you are in the driver's seat of your life
sentences.zh: 而不是被外部力量左右。

sentences.en: versus being batted around by external forces.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这些都是主题和故事。

sentences.en: And again, these are themes and stories.
sentences.zh: 没有人能完全掌控自己的生活。

sentences.en: No one is completely in control of their life.
sentences.zh: 但癌症的战争故事是一个高自主性的故事。

sentences.en: But the war story of cancer is a high agency story.
sentences.zh: 有时当人们面对真正的生存威胁时，

sentences.en: And sometimes when people are in the face of real existential threat,
sentences.zh: 被提醒自身的自主性会让人感觉良好。

sentences.en: being reminded of your agency can feel good.
sentences.zh: 所以我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: So I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 在负面经历的中途往往很难做到救赎，

sentences.en: It's often hard to do redemption in the middle of negative experiences,
sentences.zh: 尽管我认为人们一直都感到有这样做的压力。

sentences.en: though I think people feel pressure to do that all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常鼓励人们抵制急于求成的救赎冲动，

sentences.en: And so I often encourage people to resist the rush to redemption
sentences.zh: 在考虑是否存在一个救赎的结局之前，

sentences.en: and to acknowledge the real awful parts of negative experiences
sentences.zh: 先去承认负面经历中那些真正糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: before thinking about whether there's a redemptive end or not.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，你刚才谈到了自主性的重要性。

sentences.en: You talked a moment ago, Jonathan, about the importance of agency.
sentences.zh: 我想在这个话题上再多停留一会儿。

sentences.en: And I want to just stay with this for a moment longer.
sentences.zh: 许多人觉得不好的事情发生在了我身上。

sentences.en: A lot of people feel bad things happen to me.
sentences.zh: 无论是生病、受伤、失去亲人，

sentences.en: And whether that's an illness or an injury or you lose a loved one
sentences.zh: 还是你的房子被烧毁，这些事情中的许多都是降临在我们身上的外部事件。

sentences.en: or your home burns down, many of these things are external things that happen to us.
sentences.zh: 于是我们中的许多人就会觉得自己实际上是在生活的风浪中随风飘摇。

sentences.en: And many of us then feel like we are effectively buffeted around by the winds of life.
sentences.zh: 请谈谈为什么讲述故事这一行为本身可能是一种重新获得某种自主感的方式。

sentences.en: Talk a moment about how the act of storytelling itself might be a way of regaining some sense of agency.
sentences.zh: 是的，这其实是我最近一直在深入思考的一个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is actually something I've been thinking a lot about recently.
sentences.zh: 当然，吸引我进入叙事认同研究领域的原因之一，

sentences.en: Certainly one of the things that drew me to the field of studying narrative identity
sentences.zh: 就是这样一个理念：你无法总是控制发生在你身上的事，

sentences.en: was the idea that you can't always control what happens to you,
sentences.zh: 但你可以控制你对发生在你身上的事所讲述的故事。

sentences.en: but you can control the story you tell about what happens to you.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，我认为这是真的。

sentences.en: And to a large extent, I think that is true.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，正如我所说，我们既是我们生活故事的主角，也是叙述者，

sentences.en: You know, as I've said, we're both the main character and the narrator of our life story,
sentences.zh: 我们确实有自主权去讲述支持我们幸福感的故事。

sentences.en: and we do have agency to tell stories that support our well-being.
sentences.zh: 所以我一点也不想贬低这一重要性。

sentences.en: So I don't want to diminish the importance of that at all.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们的故事并非只存在于我们的脑海中，对吧？

sentences.en: But at the same time, our stories don't just exist in our heads, right?
sentences.zh: 故事是用来讲给别人听的。

sentences.en: Stories are meant to be told.
sentences.zh: 如果你讲述的关于你生活的故事没有得到其他人的认可，

sentences.en: And if you're telling a story about your life that other people don't affirm,
sentences.zh: 要继续把那个故事演绎下去其实相当困难，

sentences.en: it's actually quite hard to keep living out that story,
sentences.zh: 人们会在其中失去对自己生活故事的控制。

sentences.en: where people lose control over their life stories.
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈我们生活中的重大事件，

sentences.en: Can you talk about how the big events in our lives,
sentences.zh: 婚礼、孩子的出生、亲人的离世，

sentences.en: weddings, the birth of children, the death of loved ones,
sentences.zh: 这些如何能成为讲述污染和救赎故事的格外强大的契机吗？

sentences.en: how these might be particularly powerful occasions
sentences.zh: 是的，像这样的大事件在某种程度上，

sentences.en: to tell both contamination and redemption stories?
sentences.zh: 是在呼应一种不同类型的主导叙事。

sentences.en: Yeah, so big events like that, to a certain extent,
sentences.zh: 我们在我的领域称之为传记的文化概念，

sentences.en: play into a different kind of master narrative.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在任何特定的文化中，

sentences.en: We call this in my field the cultural concept of biography,
sentences.zh: 这通常意味着

sentences.en: which means in any given culture,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到

sentences.en: there's sort of an expected timeline of milestones.
sentences.zh: 生活里往往有着一种大家默认的人生时间表与节点。

sentences.en: And so when your life coincides with those milestones,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你的生活与这些节点不期而遇时，

sentences.en: there's a socially acceptable pressure for you to narrate those.
sentences.zh: 社会就会形成一种无形的压力，推着你去讲述这些故事。

sentences.en: So I was doing a study years ago
sentences.zh: 所以几年前我曾做过一项研究，

sentences.en: where we were reading transcripts of entire life stories.
sentences.zh: 当时我们阅读了大量完整人生故事的文字记录。

sentences.en: And my students who were working with the narratives said,
sentences.zh: 那些和我一起处理这些叙事的学生对我说：

sentences.en: I can't read another high point that is about a wedding
sentences.zh: 我实在不想再看另一个关于婚礼的巅峰时刻了，

sentences.en: or the birth of a first child.
sentences.zh: 或者关于第一个孩子出生的人生高光。

sentences.en: And it's just like, right.
sentences.zh: 当时我们的感觉就是，确实如此。

sentences.en: Those are such straightforward stories
sentences.zh: 这些都是人们非常直截了当的故事，

sentences.en: for people to point to as the high point of their life.
sentences.zh: 常常被用来当作他们人生的巅峰时刻。

sentences.en: And indeed, it is often the big moments of our lives
sentences.zh: 的确，往往正是我们生活中的那些重大时刻，

sentences.en: that serve as chapter breaks,
sentences.zh: 充当了章节的分界线，

sentences.en: that serve as anchor points in our stories.
sentences.zh: 成为了我们故事中的锚点。

sentences.en: But I also want to remind everyone
